+open Classical in
+/-- One complete oracle query, including every phase redirect, returns to
+the exact stable image of the source's oracle-answer step. Its administrative
+cost is at most twice displacement plus twice query length plus thirteen.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Concatenate full-host preparation, copy/call service and
+restoration by the public run algebra. The restored control is the oracle
+answer by `step_of_qQuery`; all other fields are those of the old source. -/
+private theorem oracleHost_query (M : FinOracleTM Bool) (C : FinTM Bool)
+    (hc : 0 < C.k) (en ex : C.State) (O : Language Bool) {x : List Bool}
+    (c : Cfg (M.k + 1) Bool M.State x) (side : Bool) (r t : ℕ)
+    (hq : c.state = some M.tm.qQuery)
+    (hb : oracleSide (c.workTapePos (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)) side)
+    (hblank : c.workTapes (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k) (r : ℤ) = none)
+    (hend : C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := []) en
+        (stateWord C.k (OracleTM.queryString c))) t =
+      Cfg.ofWords ex (stateWord C.k [decide (OracleTM.queryString c ∈ O)]))
+    (hcut : ∀ s < t, (C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := []) en
+      (stateWord C.k (OracleTM.queryString c))) s).state ≠ some ex) :
+    ∃ u ≤ 2 * (c.workTapePos (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)).natAbs +
+        2 * (OracleTM.queryString c).length + t + 13,
+      ∃ side', oracleSide ((M.tm.step O c).workTapePos (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)) side' ∧
+        (oracleHost M C hc en ex).tm.runFrom (oracleStableCfg M C c side) u =
+          oracleStableCfg M C (M.tm.step O c) side' := by
+  obtain ⟨prep, hprepTime, hprep⟩ := oracleHost_prepare M C hc en ex c side hq hb
+  have service := oracleHost_service M C hc en ex c side
+    (decide (OracleTM.queryString c ∈ O)) r t hblank hend hcut
+  obtain ⟨side', hside, restore⟩ := oracleHost_restore M C hc en ex c side
+    (decide (OracleTM.queryString c ∈ O)) (by simp [hq]) hb
+  refine ⟨(prep + (2 * (OracleTM.queryString c).length + 4 + t)) +
+    ((c.workTapePos (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)).natAbs + 4), by omega, side', ?_, ?_⟩
+  · simpa only [M.tm.step_of_qQuery O hq] using hside
+  · rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add,
+      (oracleHost M C hc en ex).tm.runFrom_add _ prep
+        (2 * (OracleTM.queryString c).length + 4 + t), hprep, service, restore,
+      M.tm.step_of_qQuery O hq]
+    by_cases hmem : OracleTM.queryString c ∈ O <;> simp [hmem]
+
+/-- The requested prefix preload reaches the stable source start in exactly
+two host steps: write the origin marker, then redirect to the source start.
+
+**Proof sketch.** The four selected local tapes start blank, including the
+query by hypothesis. Identify that R1 view with `oracleBankCfg_eq`. The one
+boot row installs the shadow marker; `oracleHost_dispatch` adds the redirect.
+R1 tape replacement and `oracleSourceCfg_initial` identify the final frame. -/
+private theorem oracleHost_initial (M : FinOracleTM Bool) (C : FinTM Bool)
+    (hc : 0 < C.k) (en ex : C.State) (x : List Bool)
+    (w : Fin (M.k + 1) → List Bool) (hw : w (Fin.last M.k) = []) :
+    (oracleHost M C hc en ex).tm.runFrom
+      (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (oracleHost M C hc en ex).tm.q₀
+        (FinTM.prefixWords (oracleHostTapes M.k C.k) w)) 2 =
+      oracleStableCfg M C (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) M.tm.q₀ w) true := by
+  let d : Cfg (oracleHostTapes M.k C.k) Bool OracleDispatch x :=
+    Cfg.ofWords .boot (FinTM.prefixWords (oracleHostTapes M.k C.k) w)
+  let localInit : Cfg 4 Bool OracleDispatch x := Cfg.ofWords .boot (fun _ => [])
+  let localDone : Cfg 4 Bool OracleDispatch x :=
+    {localInit.mapState (fun _ => OracleDispatch.ready) with
+      workTapes := Function.update localInit.workTapes 1 oracleOrigin}
+  have words (i : Fin 4) :
+      FinTM.prefixWords (oracleHostTapes M.k C.k) w (oracleSlots M.k C.k hc i) = [] := by
+    fin_cases i
+    · simpa [FinTM.prefixWords, oracleSlots, oracleSourceBank, Fin.last] using hw
+    all_goals
+      simp [FinTM.prefixWords, oracleSlots, oracleSourceBank, oracleCallBank, vhostBank] <;> omega
+  have placement : embedEmitCfg
+      ⟨oracleSlots M.k C.k hc, oracleSlots_injective M.k C.k hc⟩
+      d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] localInit = d := by
+    apply oracleBankCfg_eq oracleDispatchTM _ localInit d rfl rfl rfl
+    · intro i
+      simp [localInit, d, Cfg.ofWords, words]
+    · intro i
+      rfl
+  have boot : oracleDispatchTM.runFrom localInit 1 = localDone := by
+    change oracleDispatchTM.step localInit = _
+    simp [localInit, localDone, MultiTapeTM.step, oracleDispatchTM, oracleDispatchAction,
+      Cfg.ofWords, Cfg.mapState, oracleOrigin, Cfg.ext_iff, funext_iff, Fin.forall_fin_succ,
+      Function.update_apply]
+  have admin := oracleHost_dispatch M C hc en ex d.workTapes d.workTapePos
+    localInit localDone 1 boot .ready rfl ⟨.source, (M.tm.q₀, true)⟩ rfl (by
+      intro u hu s hs
+      have hu0 : u = 0 := by omega
+      subst u
+      have he : s = .boot := (Option.some.inj hs).symm
+      subst s
+      trivial)
+  have bootView : embedEmitCfg
+      ⟨oracleSlots M.k C.k hc, oracleSlots_injective M.k C.k hc⟩
+      d.workTapes d.workTapePos [] localDone =
+        {d.mapState (fun _ => OracleDispatch.ready) with
+          workTapes := Function.update d.workTapes (oracleSlots M.k C.k hc 1) oracleOrigin} := by
+    have mapped := congrArg (Cfg.mapState (fun _ => OracleDispatch.ready)) placement
+    change embedEmitCfg _ _ _ []
+      {(localInit.mapState (fun _ => OracleDispatch.ready)) with
+        workTapes := Function.update (localInit.mapState (fun _ => OracleDispatch.ready)).workTapes
+          1 oracleOrigin} = _
+    rw [oracleEmbed_updateTape oracleDispatchTM]
+    change (embedEmitCfg _ _ _ [] (localInit.mapState (fun _ => OracleDispatch.ready))) = _
+      at mapped
+    rw [mapped]
+    rfl
+  change (oracleHost M C hc en ex).tm.runFrom (d.mapState (Sigma.mk (β := oraclePhaseState M C) OraclePhase.dispatch)) 2 = _
+  rw [← placement, admin, bootView]
+  unfold oracleStableCfg
+  rw [oracleSourceCfg_initial]
+  rfl
+
+open Classical in
+/-- One simulated source step has a linear administrative charge at radius
+`r`, plus its actual decider charge when the source submits a query.
+
+**Proof sketch.** At a query use the complete query seam and the clean-call
+budget; displacement and query length are at most the supplied radius. Away
+from a query use the inherited off-query segment at length one. Expanding
+the products gives the common coefficient `2*a + 13`, without monotonicity. -/
+private theorem oracleHost_step (M : FinOracleTM Bool) (C : FinTM Bool)
+    (hc : 0 < C.k) (en ex : C.State) (O : Language Bool) (τ : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ℕ)
+    (hcall : ∀ z : List Bool, ∃ t ≤ a * (τ z.length + z.length + 2), 0 < t ∧
+      (∀ s < t, (C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := []) en (stateWord C.k z)) s).state ≠
+        some ex) ∧
+      C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := []) en (stateWord C.k z)) t =
+        Cfg.ofWords ex (stateWord C.k [decide (z ∈ O)]))
+    {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg (M.k + 1) Bool M.State x) (side : Bool) (r : ℕ)
+    (hb : oracleSide (c.workTapePos (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)) side)
+    (hpos : (c.workTapePos (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)).natAbs ≤ r)
+    (hlen : (OracleTM.queryString c).length ≤ r)
+    (hblank : c.workTapes (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k) (r : ℤ) = none) :
+    ∃ u ≤ (2 * a + 13) * (r + 1) + (2 * a + 13) *
+        (if c.state = some M.tm.qQuery then τ (OracleTM.queryString c).length else 0),
+      ∃ side', oracleSide ((M.tm.step O c).workTapePos (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)) side' ∧
+        (oracleHost M C hc en ex).tm.runFrom (oracleStableCfg M C c side) u =
+          oracleStableCfg M C (M.tm.step O c) side' := by
+  by_cases hq : c.state = some M.tm.qQuery
+  · obtain ⟨t, ht, _, hcut, hend⟩ := hcall (OracleTM.queryString c)
+    obtain ⟨u, hu, side', hside, hrun⟩ :=
+      oracleHost_query M C hc en ex O c side r t hq hb hblank hend hcut
+    refine ⟨u, ?_, side', hside, hrun⟩
+    have hmul := Nat.mul_le_mul_left a hlen
+    have hcharge : a * τ (OracleTM.queryString c).length ≤
+        (2 * a + 13) * τ (OracleTM.queryString c).length :=
+      Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)
+    simp only [if_pos hq]
+    ring_nf at ht hu hmul hcharge ⊢
+    omega
+  · obtain ⟨side', hside, hrun⟩ := oracleHost_offQuery M C hc en ex O c side hb 1 (by
+      intro s hs
+      have hzero : s = 0 := by omega
+      subst s
+      exact hq)
+    refine ⟨1, ?_, side', hside, hrun⟩
+    simp only [if_neg hq, mul_zero, add_zero]
+    have hmul := Nat.mul_le_mul (show 1 ≤ 2 * a + 13 from by omega)
+      (show 1 ≤ r + 1 from by omega)
+    simpa using hmul
+
+open Classical in
+/-- The complete stable-boundary simulation, including initialization.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the source horizon, extending a finite ledger by the
+actual duration supplied by `oracleHost_step`. The public radius and query-length
+contracts discharge its geometric premises. `oracleCost_sum` then charges exactly
+the queries encountered, and its constant term absorbs the two initial handovers. -/
+private theorem oracleHost_run (M : FinOracleTM Bool) (C : FinTM Bool)
+    (hc : 0 < C.k) (en ex : C.State) (O : Language Bool) (τ : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ℕ)
+    (hcall : ∀ z : List Bool, ∃ t ≤ a * (τ z.length + z.length + 2), 0 < t ∧
+      (∀ s < t, (C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := []) en (stateWord C.k z)) s).state ≠
+        some ex) ∧
+      C.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := []) en (stateWord C.k z)) t =
+        Cfg.ofWords ex (stateWord C.k [decide (z ∈ O)]))
+    (x : List Bool) (w : Fin (M.k + 1) → List Bool) (hw : w (Fin.last M.k) = [])
+    (t : ℕ) :
+    ∃ s ≤ (2 * a + 13) * (t + 1) ^ 2 + (2 * a + 13) * ∑ r ∈ Finset.range t,
+        (if (M.tm.runFrom O (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) M.tm.q₀ w) r).state =
+            some M.tm.qQuery then
+          τ (OracleTM.queryString (M.tm.runFrom O
+            (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) M.tm.q₀ w) r)).length else 0),
+      ∃ side, (oracleHost M C hc en ex).tm.runFrom
+        (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (oracleHost M C hc en ex).tm.q₀
+          (FinTM.prefixWords (oracleHost M C hc en ex).k w)) s =
+        oracleStableCfg M C (M.tm.runFrom O (Cfg.ofWords M.tm.q₀ w) t) side := by
+  classical
+  let c₀ : Cfg (M.k + 1) Bool M.State x := Cfg.ofWords M.tm.q₀ w
+  let P := oracleHost M C hc en ex
+  let d₀ : Cfg P.k Bool P.State x := Cfg.ofWords P.tm.q₀ (FinTM.prefixWords P.k w)
+  let charge : ℕ → ℕ := fun r => if (M.tm.runFrom O c₀ r).state = some M.tm.qQuery
+    then τ (OracleTM.queryString (M.tm.runFrom O c₀ r)).length else 0
+  have hblank : ∀ z, c₀.workTapes (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k) z = none := by
+    simp [c₀, Cfg.ofWords, OracleTM.queryTapeIdx, hw, FinTM.bufferTape]
+  have ledger : ∀ n, ∃ cost : ℕ → ℕ, ∃ side,
+      oracleSide ((M.tm.runFrom O c₀ n).workTapePos (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)) side ∧
+      (∀ r < n, cost r ≤ (2 * a + 13) * (r + 1) + (2 * a + 13) * charge r) ∧
+      P.tm.runFrom d₀ (2 + ∑ r ∈ Finset.range n, cost r) =
+        oracleStableCfg M C (M.tm.runFrom O c₀ n) side := by
+    intro n
+    induction n with
+    | zero =>
+      refine ⟨fun _ => 0, true, ?_, by simp, ?_⟩
+      · simp [c₀, OracleTM.runFrom, Cfg.ofWords, oracleSide]
+      · simpa [P, d₀, c₀] using oracleHost_initial M C hc en ex x w hw
+    | succ n ih =>
+      obtain ⟨cost, side, hside, hcost, hrun⟩ := ih
+      have hradius := M.tm.runFrom_radius O c₀ (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k) 0
+        (by simp [c₀, Cfg.ofWords]) (fun z _ => hblank z) n
+      have hpos : ((M.tm.runFrom O c₀ n).workTapePos
+          (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)).natAbs ≤ n := by
+        have hcast : (((M.tm.runFrom O c₀ n).workTapePos
+            (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx M.k)).natAbs : ℤ) ≤ (n : ℤ) := by
+          simpa only [Nat.zero_add, Int.natCast_natAbs] using hradius.1
+        exact_mod_cast hcast
+      have hlen := OracleTM.queryString_runFrom_length_le_of_blank M.tm O c₀ hblank rfl n
+      obtain ⟨u, hu, side', hside', hstep⟩ := oracleHost_step M C hc en ex O τ a
+        hcall (M.tm.runFrom O c₀ n) side n hside hpos hlen (hradius.2 n (by simp))
+      refine ⟨Function.update cost n u, side', ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
+      · simpa only [OracleTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'] using hside'
+      · intro r hr
+        by_cases he : r = n
+        · subst r
+          simpa [charge] using hu
+        · rw [Function.update_of_ne he]
+          exact hcost r (by omega)
+      · have hsum : ∑ r ∈ Finset.range n, Function.update cost n u r =
+            ∑ r ∈ Finset.range n, cost r := by
+          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+          intro r hr
+          exact Function.update_of_ne (Nat.ne_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hr)) _ _
+        rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, hsum, Function.update_self, ← Nat.add_assoc,
+          MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hrun]
+        simpa only [OracleTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'] using hstep
+  obtain ⟨cost, side, _, hcost, hrun⟩ := ledger t
+  refine ⟨2 + ∑ r ∈ Finset.range t, cost r, ?_, side, hrun⟩
+  have hbound := oracleCost_sum (2 * a + 13) t cost charge hcost
+  change 2 + ∑ r ∈ Finset.range t, cost r ≤
+    (2 * a + 13) * (t + 1) ^ 2 + (2 * a + 13) * ∑ r ∈ Finset.range t, charge r
+  omega
+
+end oracleHostSeams
+

+/-- The choice slot is inserted just before the query tape, leaving that tape last. -/
+private abbrev oracleChoiceSlot (k : ℕ) : Fin (k + 1 + 1) := (Fin.last k).castSucc
+
+/-- Forward a source action and consume one choice bit. This is the W2-C table
+transform: the plain bank embeddings do not consume a choice on their framed tape. -/
+private def oracleChoiceAction {k : ℕ} {S : Type} (a : Action (k + 1) Bool S) :
+    Action (k + 1 + 1) Bool (S ⊕ Fin 3) where
+  inputTape := a.inputTape
+  workTapes := Fin.insertNth (oracleChoiceSlot k) (none, 1) a.workTapes
+  output := a.output
+  state := a.state.map Sum.inl
+
+/-- The W2-C controller. The two answer pauses consume the ignored query choice;
+all blank-choice rows use the public emit-and-halt action. -/
+private def oracleChoiceMachine (N : FinOracleNDTM Bool) : FinOracleTM Bool where
+  k := N.k + 1
+  State := N.State ⊕ Fin 3
+  tm := {
+    q₀ := .inl N.tm.q₀
+    qQuery := .inl N.tm.qQuery
+    qYes := .inr 0
+    qNo := .inr 1
+    tr := fun q inp w => match w (oracleChoiceSlot N.k) with
+      | none => OracleTM.answerAction false
+      | some b => oracleChoiceAction (match q with
+        | .inl s => N.tm.tr b s inp (fun i => w ((oracleChoiceSlot N.k).succAbove i))
+        | .inr r => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none,
+            some (if r = 0 then N.tm.qYes else N.tm.qNo)⟩) }
+  wf := by constructor <;> simp
+
+/-- A source configuration with one inserted, read-only choice tape and its cursor.
+The source query tape and input head are retained verbatim. -/
+private def oracleChoiceCfg {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
+    (c : Cfg (k + 1) Bool S x) (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ) :
+    Cfg (k + 1 + 1) Bool (S ⊕ Fin 3) x where
+  state := c.state.map Sum.inl
+  inputPos := c.inputPos
+  workTapes := Fin.insertNth (oracleChoiceSlot k) tape c.workTapes
+  workTapePos := Fin.insertNth (oracleChoiceSlot k) p c.workTapePos
+  output := c.output
+
+/-- Applying the choice transform forwards all source fields and advances just
+the inserted cursor. Proof sketch: split the tape index at the inserted slot. -/
+private theorem oracleChoiceAction_apply {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
+    (a : Action (k + 1) Bool S) (c : Cfg (k + 1) Bool S x)
+    (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ) (s : Option (S ⊕ Fin 3)) :
+    (oracleChoiceAction a).apply ({oracleChoiceCfg c tape p with state := s} :
+      Cfg (k + 1 + 1) Bool (S ⊕ Fin 3) x) =
+      oracleChoiceCfg (a.apply c) tape (p + 1) := by
+  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl
+  · funext i
+    induction i using Fin.succAboveCases (oracleChoiceSlot k) <;>
+      simp [oracleChoiceAction, oracleChoiceCfg, Action.apply]
+  · funext i
+    induction i using Fin.succAboveCases (oracleChoiceSlot k) <;>
+      simp [oracleChoiceAction, oracleChoiceCfg, Action.apply]
+
+/-- Inserting the choice tape does not change the word submitted to the oracle.
+Proof sketch: the old last tape maps to the new last tape under `succAbove`. -/
+private theorem oracleChoiceCfg_query {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
+    (c : Cfg (k + 1) Bool S x) (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ) :
+    OracleTM.queryString (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) = OracleTM.queryString c := by
+  classical
+  letI : DecidableEq Bool := fun a b => Classical.propDecidable (a = b)
+  have hlast : (oracleChoiceSlot k).succAbove (Fin.last k) = Fin.last (k + 1) :=
+    Fin.succAbove_ne_last_last (Fin.castSucc_ne_last _)
+  have ht : (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p).workTapes (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx (k + 1)) =
+      c.workTapes (OracleTM.queryTapeIdx k) := by
+    change Fin.insertNth (α := fun _ => ℤ → Option Bool)
+      (oracleChoiceSlot k) tape c.workTapes (Fin.last (k + 1)) = c.workTapes (Fin.last k)
+    rw [← hlast, Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove]
+  exact congrArg (fun f : ℤ → Option Bool =>
+    if h : ∃ n : ℕ, f (n : ℤ) = none then
+      (List.range (Nat.find h)).filterMap fun n => f (n : ℤ)
+    else []) ht
+
+/-- A live nonquery step consumes a bit and forwards exactly the selected source
+action. Proof sketch: the inserted tape is absent from the source read vector;
+apply the action transport after selecting its current bit. -/
+private theorem oracleChoice_step (N : FinOracleNDTM Bool) (O : Language Bool)
+    {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg (N.k + 1) Bool N.State x)
+    (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ) (b : Bool) (q : N.State)
+    (hs : c.state = some q) (hq : q ≠ N.tm.qQuery) (hb : tape p = some b) :
+    (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.step O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) =
+      oracleChoiceCfg (N.tm.stepWith O b c) tape (p + 1) := by
+  have hread : (fun i => (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p).workTapeSymbols
+      ((oracleChoiceSlot N.k).succAbove i)) = c.workTapeSymbols := by
+    funext i
+    simp [oracleChoiceCfg, Cfg.workTapeSymbols]
+  have hbit : (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p).workTapeSymbols (oracleChoiceSlot N.k) =
+      some b := by simp [oracleChoiceCfg, Cfg.workTapeSymbols, hb]
+  simp only [OracleNDTM.stepWith, hs, if_neg hq]
+  unfold OracleTM.step
+  simp only [oracleChoiceCfg, hs, Option.map_some]
+  rw [if_neg (show (Sum.inl q : N.State ⊕ Fin 3) ≠
+      (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.qQuery from fun h => hq (Sum.inl.inj h))]
+  change (match (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p).workTapeSymbols (oracleChoiceSlot N.k) with
+    | none => OracleTM.answerAction false
+    | some b => oracleChoiceAction (N.tm.tr b q c.inputSymbol
+        (fun i => (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p).workTapeSymbols
+          ((oracleChoiceSlot N.k).succAbove i)))).apply (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) = _
+  rw [hbit, hread]
+  exact oracleChoiceAction_apply _ c tape p _
+
+/-- The answer pause consumes a present choice bit without changing any source
+tape, head or output. Proof sketch: its source action is stationary and silent. -/
+private theorem oracleChoice_pause (N : FinOracleNDTM Bool) (O : Language Bool)
+    {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg (N.k + 1) Bool N.State x)
+    (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ) (b : Bool) (r : Fin 3) (hb : tape p = some b) :
+    (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.step O
+        ({oracleChoiceCfg c tape p with state := some (.inr r)} :
+          Cfg (N.k + 1 + 1) Bool (N.State ⊕ Fin 3) x) =
+      oracleChoiceCfg
+        ({c with state := some (if r = 0 then N.tm.qYes else N.tm.qNo)} :
+          Cfg (N.k + 1) Bool N.State x) tape (p + 1) := by
+  unfold OracleTM.step
+  simp only [oracleChoiceMachine, Sum.inr_ne_inl, ↓reduceIte]
+  simp only [Cfg.workTapeSymbols, oracleChoiceCfg, Fin.insertNth_apply_same, hb]
+  simpa only [Action.apply, moveInputPos_zero, SignType.coe_zero, add_zero, Option.toList_none,
+    List.append_nil] using oracleChoiceAction_apply
+      (⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none, some (if r = 0 then N.tm.qYes else N.tm.qNo)⟩ :
+        Action (N.k + 1) Bool N.State) c tape p (some (.inr r))
+
+/-- A query step is implemented by the oracle answer and its one-bit pause.
+Proof sketch: cite the public query step on the host and on the fixed-choice
+source; query-word preservation makes the two oracle tests identical. -/
+private theorem oracleChoice_queryStep (N : FinOracleNDTM Bool) (O : Language Bool)
+    {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg (N.k + 1) Bool N.State x)
+    (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ) (b : Bool)
+    (hs : c.state = some N.tm.qQuery) (hb : tape p = some b) :
+    (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.runFrom O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) 2 =
+      oracleChoiceCfg (N.tm.stepWith O b c) tape (p + 1) := by
+  classical
+  rw [show 2 = 1 + 1 from rfl, OracleTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
+  change (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.step O
+    ((oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.step O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p)) = _
+  rw [OracleTM.step_of_qQuery _ O (cfg := oracleChoiceCfg c tape p)
+      (by simp [oracleChoiceCfg, hs, oracleChoiceMachine]),
+    oracleChoiceCfg_query, OracleNDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step,
+    (N.tm.fixChoice b).step_of_qQuery O (cfg := c) hs]
+  by_cases h : OracleTM.queryString c ∈ O
+  · simp only [if_pos h]
+    exact oracleChoice_pause N O c tape p b 0 hb
+  · simp only [if_neg h]
+    simpa only [show (1 : Fin 3) ≠ 0 from by decide, ↓reduceIte] using
+      oracleChoice_pause N O c tape p b 1 hb
+
+/-- A blank choice cell in any nonquery live state appends `false` and halts.
+Proof sketch: select the public `answerAction false` row at the actual read. -/
+private theorem oracleChoice_blank (N : FinOracleNDTM Bool) (O : Language Bool)
+    {x : List Bool} (d : Cfg (N.k + 1 + 1) Bool (N.State ⊕ Fin 3) x)
+    (q : N.State ⊕ Fin 3) (hs : d.state = some q) (hq : q ≠ .inl N.tm.qQuery)
+    (hb : d.workTapeSymbols (oracleChoiceSlot N.k) = none) :
+    (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.step O d =
+      {d with state := none, output := d.output ++ [false]} := by
+  unfold OracleTM.step
+  simp only [hs]
+  rw [if_neg (show q ≠ (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.qQuery from hq)]
+  change (match d.workTapeSymbols (oracleChoiceSlot N.k) with
+    | none => OracleTM.answerAction false
+    | some b => oracleChoiceAction (match q with
+      | .inl s => N.tm.tr b s d.inputSymbol
+          (fun i => d.workTapeSymbols ((oracleChoiceSlot N.k).succAbove i))
+      | .inr r => ⟨0, fun _ => (none, 0), none,
+          some (if r = 0 then N.tm.qYes else N.tm.qNo)⟩)).apply d = _
+  rw [hb]
+  exact Cfg.ext rfl (moveInputPos_zero _) rfl (funext fun _ => add_zero _) rfl
+
+/-- Exhaustion takes at most two steps, including exhaustion at a query state.
+Proof sketch: a halted source needs no steps; a live ordinary state takes the
+blank-choice action; a query state first answers and then takes that same action. -/
+private theorem oracleChoice_exhaust (N : FinOracleNDTM Bool) (O : Language Bool)
+    {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg (N.k + 1) Bool N.State x)
+    (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ) (hb : tape p = none) :
+    ∃ s ≤ 2,
+      ((oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.runFrom O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) s).state = none ∧
+      ((oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.runFrom O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) s).output =
+        if c.state = none then c.output else c.output ++ [false] := by
+  classical
+  have hblank : (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p).workTapeSymbols (oracleChoiceSlot N.k) =
+      none := by simp [oracleChoiceCfg, Cfg.workTapeSymbols, hb]
+  cases hs : c.state with
+  | none => exact ⟨0, by omega, by simp [OracleTM.runFrom, oracleChoiceCfg, hs]⟩
+  | some q =>
+    by_cases hq : q = N.tm.qQuery
+    · subst q
+      refine ⟨2, le_rfl, ?_⟩
+      have hrun : (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.runFrom O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) 2 =
+          {oracleChoiceCfg c tape p with state := none, output := c.output ++ [false]} := by
+        change (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.step O
+          ((oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.step O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p)) = _
+        rw [OracleTM.step_of_qQuery _ O (cfg := oracleChoiceCfg c tape p)
+          (by simp [oracleChoiceCfg, hs, oracleChoiceMachine])]
+        split_ifs <;>
+          exact oracleChoice_blank N O _ _ rfl (by simp [oracleChoiceMachine])
+            (by exact hblank)
+      rw [hrun]
+      simp
+    · refine ⟨1, by omega, ?_⟩
+      have hrun : (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.runFrom O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) 1 =
+          {oracleChoiceCfg c tape p with state := none, output := c.output ++ [false]} :=
+        oracleChoice_blank N O _ (.inl q) (by simp [oracleChoiceCfg, hs])
+          (fun h => hq (Sum.inl.inj h)) hblank
+      rw [hrun]
+      simp
+
+/-- Lockstep along a finite choice suffix, charging one step ordinarily and two
+at a query, followed by the exhaustion tail.
+
+**Proof sketch.** Induct on the suffix, generalizing the source configuration and
+the choice cursor, as in `OracleTM.toOracleNDTM_runWith`. A halted configuration
+absorbs the suffix. Otherwise one of the two local correspondence lemmas supplies
+the next source configuration; compose with the induction hypothesis using the
+public run algebra. The read invariant shifts by one, without changing the tape. -/
+private theorem oracleChoice_run (N : FinOracleNDTM Bool) (O : Language Bool)
+    {x : List Bool} (u : List Bool) (c : Cfg (N.k + 1) Bool N.State x)
+    (tape : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ)

+    ∃ s ≤ 2 * u.length + 2,
+      ((oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.runFrom O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) s).state = none ∧
+      ((oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.runFrom O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) s).output =
+        if (N.tm.runWith O u c).state = none then (N.tm.runWith O u c).output
+        else (N.tm.runWith O u c).output ++ [false] := by

+  induction u generalizing c p with
+  | nil => exact oracleChoice_exhaust N O c tape p (by simpa using hread 0)
+  | cons b u ih =>

+    | none =>

+      rw [OracleNDTM.runWith_of_halt O c hs]
+      simp [OracleTM.runFrom, oracleChoiceCfg, hs]
+    | some q =>
+      have hb : tape p = some b := by simpa using hread 0

+          (oracleChoiceMachine N).tm.runFrom O (oracleChoiceCfg c tape p) d =
+            oracleChoiceCfg (N.tm.stepWith O b c) tape (p + 1) := by
+        by_cases hq : q = N.tm.qQuery

+/-- Loading the one choice word is exactly the transport of the source's initial

+private theorem oracleChoice_initial (N : FinOracleNDTM Bool) (x u : List Bool) :

+  · funext i
+    induction i using Fin.succAboveCases (oracleChoiceSlot N.k) <;>
+      simp [Cfg.ofWords, oracleChoiceCfg]

import Lean.Util.FoldConsts
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputLength
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.CertShell
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.OracleSim
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassOracle.Classes
open Lean Elab Command in
/-- Every constant in the dependency closure of `root` whose own type or value
mentions `sorryAx` (maintainer's read-only admission walk). -/
def sorrySourcesOf (env : Environment) (root : Name) : Array Name := Id.run do
  let mut visited : NameSet := {}
  let mut stack : Array Name := #[root]
  let mut srcs : Array Name := #[]
  while !stack.isEmpty do
    let c := stack.back!
    stack := stack.pop
    if visited.contains c then continue
    visited := visited.insert c
    if let some ci := env.find? c then
      let used := ci.getUsedConstantsAsSet
      if used.contains ``sorryAx then srcs := srcs.push c
      for d in used.toList do
        unless visited.contains d do stack := stack.push d
  return srcs

open Lean Elab Command in
elab "#sorry_sources " id:ident : command => do
  let n ← liftCoreM <| realizeGlobalConstNoOverload id
  logInfo m!"{n}: direct sorryAx users in closure: {sorrySourcesOf (← getEnv) n}"

open Lean Elab Command in
/-- Every constant whose name starts with the given string (a module's private prefix), and
those among them whose own type or value mentions `sorryAx` (maintainer's read-only census). -/
elab "#private_sorry_census " pre:str : command => do
  let env ← getEnv
  let p := pre.getString
  let mut n := 0
  let mut bad : Array Name := #[]
  for (c, ci) in env.constants.toList do
    if (toString c).startsWith p then
      n := n + 1
      if ci.getUsedConstantsAsSet.contains ``sorryAx then bad := bad.push c
  logInfo m!"{p}: {n} constants; direct sorryAx users: {bad}"

## ===== audits/evidence/retrofit/copy-text-screen.py (at the gate head) =====

```
"""Text-level copy screen for retrofit deliveries (introduced after RB4).

Declaration counts can be satisfied by inlining a copy into its consumer.
This screen measures copied *text* instead. For the given Lean files it lists
every like-kind pair (proof vs proof, term vs term) in which one declaration
reproduces at least half of another's extracted body (at least 60 characters,
greedy tiling with blocks of at least 25), within a file and across the given
files. It also prints the total reproduced text. Run it before and after a
change: a pair present after but not before is new duplication; inlining a
deleted copy into a consumer shows up as such a pair.
Usage: python3 -I copy-text-screen.py <repo-root> <file.lean> [<file.lean> ...]
"""
import re, sys
root, files = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
def strip(src):
    out = []; i = 0; depth = 0; n = len(src)
    while i < n:
        if src.startswith('/-', i): depth += 1; i += 2; continue
        if depth and src.startswith('-/', i): depth -= 1; i += 2; continue
        if depth: i += 1; continue
        if src.startswith('--', i):
            j = src.find('\n', i); i = n if j < 0 else j; continue
        out.append(src[i]); i += 1
    return ''.join(out)
DECL = re.compile(r"^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?((?:(?:noncomputable|private|protected)\s+)*)"
                  r"(def|theorem|lemma|abbrev|instance|structure|inductive)\s+(\S+)", re.M)
def body(b):
    d = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(b):
        if ch in '([{⟨': d += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩': d -= 1
        elif b.startswith(':=', i) and d == 0: return b[i + 2:]
    d = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(b):
        if ch in '([{⟨': d += 1
        elif ch in ')]}⟩': d -= 1
        elif d == 0 and (ch == '|' or re.match(r'\bwhere\b', b[i:i + 6])): return b[i:]
    return ''
def lcs(a, b):
    lo, hi, best = 0, min(len(a), len(b)), ''
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
        subs = {b[i:i + mid] for i in range(len(b) - mid + 1)}
        hit = next((a[i:i + mid] for i in range(len(a) - mid + 1) if a[i:i + mid] in subs), None)
        if hit is not None: lo, best = mid, hit
        else: hi = mid - 1
    return lo, best
def tiled(a, b):
    c = 0
    while True:
        n, seg = lcs(a, b)
        if n < 25: return c
        c += n; a = a.replace(seg, '\x00', 1); b = b.replace(seg, '\x01', 1)
grams = lambda x: {x[i:i + 25] for i in range(len(x) - 24)}
decls = []
for f in files:
    t = strip(open(f'{root}/{f}', encoding='utf-8').read()); ms = list(DECL.finditer(t))
    for i, m in enumerate(ms):
        end = ms[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(ms) else len(t)
        kind = 'proof' if m.group(2) in ('theorem', 'lemma') else 'term'
        bd = re.sub(r'\s+', '', body(t[m.start():end]))
        if len(bd) >= 60: decls.append((f.split('/')[-1], m.group(3), kind, bd, grams(bd)))
pairs = []; total = 0
for (fa, a, ka, ta, ga) in decls:
    for (fb, b, kb, tb, gb) in decls:
        if (fa, a) == (fb, b) or ka != kb or not (ga & gb): continue
        sh = tiled(tb, ta)
        if sh >= 60 and 2 * sh >= len(tb):
            pairs.append((sh / len(tb), sh, len(tb), f'{fa}::{a}', f'{fb}::{b}')); total += sh
pairs.sort(reverse=True)
print(f"declarations screened: {len(decls)}; copy pairs (target reproduces >= half of source): {len(pairs)}; reproduced text: {total:,} chars")
for frac, sh, ln, a, b in pairs:
    print(f"   {a}  reproduces  {b}: {sh}/{ln} = {frac:.0%}")
```

## ===== backlog.md (at the gate head) =====

# Backlog

The consolidated tracking file for the Arora-Barak campaign branch
(`complexity/arora-barak-ch1`) and adjacent repository work: human-review
design questions, queued and on-hold campaign work, deferred formalizations,
pending decisions, and housekeeping. Consolidated 2026-09-18 from the two
campaign plans, the audit resolutions records, and session assessments.

**Conventions.** This file is the *canonical home* of the human-review
question statements (§1) — the plans keep stable numbered stubs, since audit
documents cite the numbering — and the *tracking index* for everything else
(scope prose remains in the plans; decision-log history is never moved).
New items land here; an item leaves only by a decision recorded in the
relevant plan's decision log. From the next audit round onward this file
joins the bundle attachment set.

---

## 1. Human-review design questions (reserved — never closed by an automated gate)

Flagged for a **human** auditor/maintainer: the LLM audit rounds verify
correctness, but these are matters of architectural taste and trust-surface
policy.

### CH1-Q1 — the 3A Mathlib-computability bridge

*Origin: `AroraBarakChapter1Plan.md` §5 (epoch 3, batch A);
`MathlibBridge.lean`, `Turing.exists_effectiveMachineCode`.*

The audited docstring sketch called for the canonizer machine to be
**hand-assembled from this repository's composition combinators** ("its
construction uses the composition combinators", optionally with a polynomial
`canonizerTime`). The delivered proof instead (i) proves the canonization
*function* primitive recursive, (ii) compiles it through **Mathlib's verified
recursion-theory pipeline** (`ToPartrec.Code.exists_code` →
`PartrecToTM2.tr_eval`), (iii) simulates the resulting TM2 stack machine in
our model with a bespoke private `bridgeTM`, and (iv) lands in the binary
alphabet via the proved `alphabet_reduction`, extracting the time bound by
finite maxima (no polynomial bound claimed — permitted, since
`canonizerTime` is existential). The batch flagged the deviation itself; the
maintainer verification pass confirmed the proof is sorry-free with the
standard axiom footprint and zero public-interface drift. **Open questions
for a human:** (a) is the heavyweight `Mathlib.Computability.TMToPartrec`
import into the TM tree acceptable, or should the bridge be quarantined
behind the planned phase-5 `MathlibBridge` module boundary (it effectively
front-runs that module)? (b) is the enlarged trust/review surface (Mathlib's
TM2 semantics + the private `bridgeTM` simulation, ~150 private
declarations) preferable to a longer but self-contained combinator
construction? (c) should the abandoned polynomial-`canonizerTime` claim be
recorded as permanently out of scope, or re-derived later from the
combinator route if one is ever written? Since the epoch-3→4 merge the
bridge lives in the dedicated `MathlibBridge.lean`, which implements the
quarantine that part (a) contemplates — the `TMToPartrec` import is confined
to that one module and nothing outside `exists_effectiveMachineCode` depends
on it — but the implemented quarantine does **not** dispose of this
question: parts (a)-(c) remain open for human review (epoch-4 audit,
finding 3: an earlier version of this text misplaced the bridge inside
`Encoding.lean`).

*Cross-link: part (c) gained relevance in Chapter 2 — see §3, "Polynomial
canonizer for a concrete scheme".*

### CH1-Q2 — the 3B universal-interpreter proof architecture

*Origin: `AroraBarakChapter1Plan.md` §5 (epoch 3, batches B + B2);
`Universal.lean`, `Turing.universal`.*

The proof followed the audited sketch's outline (prefix-only startup,
canonizer capture onto a table tape, four-work-tape interpreter with a fixed
finite controller), but the realized architecture is by far the campaign's
most involved artifact: 2465 lines (2831 after the epoch-4A timed fill), 104
private declarations built across two agent sessions (WIP `f191b918` +
continuation), a bespoke checkpoint relation (`universalRelation`) with
generic block-simulation assembly (`universal_block_run` /
`universal_from_blocks`), a virtual left boundary via a marker tape, a unary
state tape with group-wise table scanning, and an *exact* per-phase cost
ledger realized to `universalBlockBound = 3L + 5N + 20`. The kernel checks
all of it, and the public statement is frozen and audited — but the *design*
was never itself an audit deliverable at this level of detail. **Open
questions for a human:** (a) is this the right load-bearing shape — and
which parts (the capture wrapper, the block-run/`universal_run_join`
assembly, the marker-directed rewind and unary-copy gadget patterns, all
flagged by the agents as promotion candidates) should graduate to shared
modules rather than being re-derived? (b) is the exact-ledger posture
(`3L + 5N + 20` proved to the transition) worth its brittleness against any
future change to `CodeTM.serialize`, or should the maintained invariant be
an existential bound with the exact ledger demoted to documentation? (c)
does the interpreter's claim to *be* the book's universal machine (as
opposed to satisfying the frozen statement, which the kernel settles)
deserve a targeted human read of the construction's core definitions
(`UniversalControl`, `universalInterpreter`, `universalRelation`), given no
executable diagnostics of the whole interpreter ever ran (the batch-B smoke
tests aborted on deep recursion and were discarded)?

### U-1: re-derive the chapter-1 universal machine from B5a's generic step block (user, 2026-10-11)

*Merged with MIG-2 (user, 2026-10-12): the timed-layer dedup and this re-derivation are one migration item.*

The chapter-1 universal machine (`Turing.universal`, `universal_quadratic`, `timed_universal`) is
a bespoke interpreter of about 5,300 lines across `Universal.lean`, `UniversalStartup.lean`,
`UniversalInterpreter.lean` and `UniversalBlock.lean`. It is hard-wired to one work tape, and it
is already copied once: the timed form carries its own private stopped-interpreter layer. B5a
(`briefs/b5a-fill.md`, design §12.11) builds one format-parameterized interpreter instead. That
is a single private step block for one simulated transition of a `k`-tape coded table, whose
per-round cost is independent of `t` and `x`.

**The item:** after B5a lands, re-derive the three chapter-1 statements from that step block, and
delete the bespoke interpreter layers.

**H1 alone does not suffice.** The frozen statements need what B5a's headline does not give:
- **full output:** `universal` computes `M_α(x)`, and `timed_universal` emits `true :: output`,
  whereas H1 answers only `[true]`/`[false]` from a silent output summary;
- **a per-code linear bound with no `|x|` term:** `universal` is `C(α)·(t + 1)` and
  `timed_universal` is `C(α)·(t + 1)²`, whereas H1 is a polynomial in `|α| + |x| + t`;
- **no deadline, and divergence preserved:** `universal` runs until halt, and its converse says
  every completed output of `U` is one of the simulated machine's.

**Route.** Reuse the step block under new hosts. The natural route is H2 above (the per-code
linear timed simulator, with its suffix-input host), plus an emitting variant of the block's
output handling and an unclocked loop host for `universal`. Keep all three statements unchanged;
`UniversalStartup`'s public input pieces (`universalInput_read`/`_move`) are the suffix-input
host's components.

**Governance.** A 12.2c item: its own PR and gate. The chapter-1 statements are frozen, and every
consumer of `universal`/`timed_universal` is re-checked. Prerequisite: the B5a fill (H1's step
block proved). *Origin: B5a design discussion; user, 2026-10-11.*

## 2. Campaign work queued or on hold

### MIG / RS: the foundation migration and the restyling backlog (user, 2026-10-12; design §16)

The user lifted the no-retroactive-migration rules for this work and chose scenario B. Duplicate
statement families are retired, with full gates and consumer edits. Restyling is opportunistic:
**pick any row whose prerequisites are met.** The estimates come from seven read-only reviews
(design §16), in lines, and are ESTIMATED unless marked; negative means saved.

**Gates:**
- **swap:** statements are unchanged, so a freeze check, a replay and a fidelity gate;
- **stmt:** new public statements, so a statement gate;

* **Machine-routine layer (user decision 2026-10-06: build once
  chapter 2 is done, in the E5-closure/D7 window, before chapter 3).**
  Three pieces, sized by the A-chain's evidence (≈ half of the A2/A3
  deliveries' 202 native privates are hand-rebuilt universal routines;
  `emitterBank*`/`emitterP2*` relocation privately re-harvested three
  times; A3's proved costs `3|w|+3` copy / `2|w|+2` clear match the
  prior art's `3w+2`/`2w+2` to within one step):
  1. a generic **bank-embedding theorem** — a verified routine on its
     own small tape set runs on any selected tape subset of a `k`-tape
     machine, cost unchanged, all other tapes/heads framed (the public
     generic form of `emitterBank*`/`clBank*`/`clSlot*`);
  2. a generic **seam-composition lemma** — sequential composition of
     two controllers at a canonical `Cfg.ofWords` seam with first-return
     cuts and additive budgets (the generic form of the per-batch
     dispatch gluing);
  3. **catalog promotion** of transfer/clear/copy/compare/increment as
     public machines with exact costs, seeded from the already-audited
     A-chain privates (D6-style promotion, not new proof work).
  **Survey update 2026-10-06 (pre-§12, recorded ahead of the

  per entry produced zero. Fix: state the per-entry function-call check
  as a hard requirement in `.claude/agents/blueprint-writer.md` (and
  ideally add a `--chapter` mode to the scripts). The orchestrator-side
  uniform pass used here (`build_dataset.parse_blueprint` + both checks,

### Chapters 2-3

  problems) — each needs a graph/arithmetic encoding surface; the legacy
  `Complexity/NPReductions/*` files may eventually be **retargeted** as the

* **Ex 2.30, Berman's theorem.** *Origin: ch2 plan §1.*
* **General Boolean formulas** — `TAUTOLOGY` is deliberately stated on the
  documented DNF fragment; a general-formula carrier (AST, evaluation,
  serialization) is new work, and any future general `TAUTOLOGY` must not be
  silently identified with the fragment. *Origin: ch2 phase-3/4 audits.*
* **`MathlibBridge` poly-time upgrade** (open lever): `bridgeTM` costs O(1)
  native steps per TM2 operation, so a Mathlib `TM2ComputableInPolyTime`
  certificate would transfer. (The Chapter-6 bridges were built on native
  machines without it; see §3.)
  *Origin: ch2 plan decision log ("revisit at phase 3" — still open).*
* **Oracle complexity classes** (Chapter 3): `Oracle.lean` has the raw model
  and both lockstep embeddings, audited; the class layer, the
  persistent-vs-auto-erased query-tape statement (polynomial overhead only —
  constant overhead provably impossible), and relativization (Baker-Gill-
  Solovay) are future Chapter-3 work. *Origin: ch1 plan §5 phase-2 notes;
  session assessment 2026-09-18.*
* **B5a headline H2: the per-code-linear timed simulator** (user, 2026-10-11:
  "H1 for now, but add H2 to backlog"). `CodeSimulator.lean`'s headline is
  H1, polynomial in `|α| + |x| + t` jointly, which is exactly what the two
  uniform schemes need. **H2** gives the same verdicts within
  `d · (|α| + 1)^d · (t + 1)`, with no `|x|` term and linear in `t` per
  code. It would make the one interpreter the stage-1 timed universal at
  linear overhead. It needs a **suffix-input host**: the simulated machine
  reads `x` in place inside the native input, behind a left-boundary
  marker. The pieces are public (`universalInput_read`/`_move`,
  `UniversalStartup.lean`), but no host composes them. H2 ⇒ H1 is already
  proved (`exists_uniformSimulator_of_timed`, B5a statement probe), so H2
  can later be added beside H1 without disturbing its consumers. The step
  block's per-round cost is independent of `t` and `x`, so the B5a fill's
  trace is the H2 core. H2 is also the natural route for 12.2c item **U-1** (§1).
  *Origin: B5a dossier D3; design §12.11.*

import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.CfgRecord

import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Bitwise

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

/-!
# Machine-construction library: record tables and the deferred record rows (§12.8b)

The table layer of the §12.8 rich-alphabet design and the record rows its
statement gate deferred (`machine-library-design.md` §12.8a §8 item 10, §9
decisions 2 and 5, §12.8b). A **table** is a header field followed by entries,
each entry a fixed number of fields, all in the blank-separated field layout of
`Turing.joinFields`, with two blank cells on each side. The breadth-first
simulation of `NSPACE` in exponential time keeps its visited set in one; the
rows here append to a table, find the first entry a finite-state fold accepts,
copy field lists between tapes, and return from a table's end to its start.
The record rows write the record template and the initial record from binary
radius digits, decide record validity against the template, and enumerate the
valid records, which Savitch's midpoint recursion consumes.

**Status: partial fill (14 of 20 targets proved).** The layout facts, the
end-to-start adapter and field-list copy are proved. Six existential rows remain
sorried with their proof sketches. Append also has a proved reverse copier and
seek-and-copy prefix. The already-landed `Turing.RecordValid.joinFields_length`
is admission-free as well.

## Design

* **The table layout** (decision 2 of §12.8a §9). `Turing.tableFields h es`
  is the header `h` followed by the fields of the entries `es`, and
  `Turing.TableAt` places its layout at an origin with two blank cells before
  the header and two after the last field. The header is nonempty, so the
  field list is never empty, every seek precondition is uniform, and the
  empty table is a header alone. Entries are addressed by
  `Turing.tableOffset`, the cell their first field starts at.
* **The end-to-start adapter** (decision 2, round-1 notes 14 and 42) is a real
  machine, `Turing.tableRewindTM`: skip back over the last field, then seek
  the start. Its exact framed contract is the composition of the two Catalog
  rows by one seam.
* **Find takes fuel.** The number of entries is not on any tape, and the one
  rich loop host, `Turing.counterLoopTMVia`, runs a counter, so
  `Turing.exists_tableFindTM` takes a digit word whose value exceeds the
  number of entries and restores it. The breadth-first host keeps one such word.
* **Field-list copy** `Turing.exists_fieldsCopyTM` moves a fixed number of
  fields between tapes; append and the enumeration are built on it, and the
  hosts use it for workspaces, table entries and Savitch's frames.
* **Record rows are existential modules** in the house style: a machine,
  entry and verdict anchors with `yes ≠ no`, a first-return time bound, an
  exact finish configuration that restores every head, the input position and
  the scratch, and a work-space clause bounding every work head through the
  verdict to `C·(size + 1)` cells of its entry position (round-1 major 1).
  Tape layouts are fixed and local, hosted by R1 (decision 4).
* **The template** `Turing.recordTemplate n s` carries what a record row cannot
  read off a candidate: the bound `n + 1` at the position width, and the
  `2s + 1`-cell window of a blank tape with its head at `0`.
* **The enumeration order is existential.** `Turing.exists_recordNextTM`
  exports a duplicate-free list of exactly the valid records and a module that
  walks it; the order the fill realizes is the odometer order, but no consumer
  reads it.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.recordLength` — the layout length of every record at `(k, n, s)`.
* `Turing.recordTemplate` — the widths template of the validity and
  enumeration rows.
* `Turing.tableFields`, `Turing.tableOffset`, `Turing.TableWF`,
  `Turing.TableAt` — the table layout, entry offsets, well-formedness, and
  placement on a tape.
* `Turing.tableRewindTM` — the end-to-start adapter.

## Main results

* `Turing.joinFields_length`, `Turing.fieldOffset_length`,
  `Turing.joinFields_cfgRecord_length`, `Turing.cfgRecord_field_ne_nil`,
  `Turing.cfgRecord_init`, `Turing.RecordValid.joinFields_length`,
  `Turing.recordValid_iff_exists_cfg`,
  `Turing.joinFields_recordTemplate_length`, `Turing.binDigits_posWidth_succ`
  — layout and record facts (proved).
* `Turing.TableWF.field_ne_nil`, `Turing.tableOffset_eq`,
  `Turing.tableOffset_length`, `Turing.TableAt.recordAt_take` — table facts
  (proved).
* `Turing.tableRewindTM_run_ofCfg` — the adapter's framed contract
  (proved).
* `Turing.exists_fieldsCopyTM` — field-list copy (proved).
* `Turing.exists_tableFindTM`, `Turing.exists_tableAppendTM` — the remaining
  table rows (statements).
* `Turing.exists_recordTemplateTM`, `Turing.exists_recordInitTM`,
  `Turing.exists_recordValidTM`, `Turing.exists_recordNextTM` — the deferred
  record rows of R8.7 (statements).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1 and Claim 4.4: configurations
  described in `O(S(n))` bits; Theorem 4.2(iii), whose simulation searches the
  configuration graph keeping a table of visited configurations; Theorem 4.14
  (Savitch), whose recursion enumerates candidate midpoint configurations.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-! ### Layout lengths -/

/-- **The length of a field layout** (design §12.8b). A nonempty field list
lays out as its cells plus one separator between consecutive fields.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the list: `List.intercalate` of a singleton is its
field, and each further field adds its length and one separator.

**Fill appendix.** Reuse the public layout induction in
`Turing.length_joinFields_add_one`; the remaining induction distributes the
sum of field lengths plus one. No second layout induction is introduced. -/
theorem joinFields_length {Γ : Type*} (fs : List (List Γ)) (hfs : fs ≠ []) :
    (joinFields fs).length = (fs.map List.length).sum + fs.length - 1 := by
  have h := length_joinFields_add_one fs hfs
  have hs : (fs.map (fun u => u.length + 1)).sum =
      (fs.map List.length).sum + fs.length := by
    clear h hfs
    induction fs with
    | nil => simp
    | cons u fs ih => simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, List.length_cons]; omega
  simp only [fieldOffset, List.take_length] at h
  omega

/-- **The end offset of a field layout** (design §12.8b; the formula of
`Turing.fieldOffset`'s docstring, made a lemma). For a nonempty field list,
`fieldOffset fs |fs|` is the layout length plus one: the cell after the blank
that ends the layout, where `Turing.seekEndTM` stops and a further field would
start.

**Proof sketch.** `fieldOffset fs |fs|` sums `|f| + 1` over all fields, which is
`Turing.joinFields_length` plus one. -/
theorem fieldOffset_length {Γ : Type*} (fs : List (List Γ)) (hfs : fs ≠ []) :
    fieldOffset fs fs.length = (joinFields fs).length + 1 := by
  exact (length_joinFields_add_one fs hfs).symm

/-- **The record length** (design §12.8b): the layout length of every record
with `k` tapes, input length `n` and radius `s` — `k` tape fields of `2s + 1`
cells, `posWidth n` position digits, the state and tag cells, and `k + 2`
separators. -/
def recordLength (k n s : ℕ) : ℕ := k * (2 * s + 1) + posWidth n + k + 4

/-- **Every record has the record length** (design §12.8b). The layout of
`Turing.cfgRecord s c τ` has length `Turing.recordLength k |x| s`, whatever the
configuration and the tag. So the valid records at `(k, n, s)` all occupy the
same interval, and a row may rewrite one record into another in place.

**Proof sketch.** `Turing.joinFields_length` with the field lengths read off
`Turing.cfgRecord`: `1`, `posWidth |x|` (`binDigits` has its width), `2s + 1`
for each of the `k` tape fields, and `1`, over `k + 3` fields. -/
theorem joinFields_cfgRecord_length {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ)
    (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T) :
    (joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length = recordLength k x.length s := by
  rw [joinFields_length _ (by simp [cfgRecord]), cfgRecord_length]
  simp only [cfgRecord, Bind.bind, Pure.pure, ← List.map_eq_flatMap,
    binDigits, List.map_cons, List.map_append, List.map_map,
    Function.comp_def, List.length_map, List.length_range, List.map_const',
    List.length_finRange, List.sum_cons, List.sum_append, List.sum_replicate_nat,
    List.length_cons, List.length_nil, List.map_nil, List.sum_nil, recordLength]
  omega

/-- **Record fields are nonempty** (design §12.8b). No field of a record is
empty, so a table of records has no double blank inside it and the seek rows
apply.

**Proof sketch.** The state and tag fields have one cell, the tape fields
`2s + 1`, and the position field `posWidth |x| ≥ 1` cells, since
`Nat.bits (|x| + 1)` is nonempty. -/
theorem cfgRecord_field_ne_nil {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ)
    (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T) : ∀ u ∈ cfgRecord s c τ, u ≠ [] := by
  have hwidth : 0 < posWidth x.length := by
    simpa only [posWidth, Nat.size_eq_bits_len] using
      (Nat.size_pos.mpr (Nat.succ_pos x.length))
  intro u hu
  simp only [cfgRecord, List.mem_cons, List.mem_append, List.mem_map,
    List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hu
  rcases hu with rfl | rfl | ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ | rfl
  · simp
  · intro h
    have := congrArg List.length h
    simp only [List.length_map, binDigits, List.length_range, List.length_nil] at this
    omega
  · intro h
    have := congrArg List.length h
    simp only [Bind.bind, Pure.pure, ← List.map_eq_flatMap,
      List.length_map, List.length_range, List.length_nil] at this
    omega
  · simp

/-- **The initial record** (design §12.8b). The record of the start
configuration `Cfg.init q₀ x` with tag `τ₀`: the state `some q₀`, the input
position `1` in `posWidth |x|` digits, `k` copies of the blank window with the
mark at its center (the head at cell `0`), and the tag. This is what
`Turing.exists_recordInitTM` writes.

**Proof sketch.** Unfold `Turing.cfgRecord` at `Cfg.init`: its work tapes are
blank, its heads at `0`, which is window index `s`, and its input position
is `1`. -/
theorem cfgRecord_init {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} (x : List Bool) (s : ℕ) (q₀ : Q) (τ₀ : T) :
    cfgRecord s (Cfg.init q₀ x : Cfg k Bool Q x) τ₀ =
      [RecSym.st (some q₀)] :: ((binDigits (posWidth x.length) 1).map RecSym.digit) ::
        (List.replicate k ((List.range (2 * s + 1)).map fun j =>
            RecSym.cell none (decide (j = s))) ++
          [[RecSym.tag τ₀]]) := by
  have hmark (j : ℕ) : (0 : ℤ) = (j : ℤ) - s ↔ j = s := by omega
  simp only [cfgRecord, Cfg.init, Bind.bind, Pure.pure,
    ← List.map_eq_flatMap, List.map_map, Function.comp_def, hmark, List.map_const',
    List.length_finRange, Fin.val_one]

/-- **Valid records have the record length** (design §12.8b).

**Proof sketch.** A valid record is `Turing.cfgRecord s c τ` for a
configuration on an input of length `n`; apply
`Turing.joinFields_cfgRecord_length`. -/
theorem RecordValid.joinFields_length {k n s : ℕ} {Q T : Type}
    {fs : List (List (RecSym Q T))} (h : RecordValid k n s Q T fs) :
    (joinFields fs).length = recordLength k n s := by
  obtain ⟨x, c, τ, hx, -, rfl⟩ := h
  rw [joinFields_cfgRecord_length, hx]

/-- **Validity over a given input** (design §12.8b). A field list is a valid
record at input length `|x|` exactly when it is the record of a windowed
configuration on `x` itself. A record depends on its input only through the
input's length, so the windowed configurations of the actual input enumerate
every valid record; Savitch's midpoint enumeration rests on this.

**Proof sketch.** Backward: take the input `x`. Forward: a configuration on an
input `x'` with `|x'| = |x|` transports to `x` with the same state, work tapes,
heads and output and the input position cast along `|x'| = |x|`; its record and
window predicate are unchanged, since neither reads the input's symbols. -/
theorem recordValid_iff_exists_cfg {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} (s : ℕ) (x : List Bool)
    (fs : List (List (RecSym Q T))) :
    RecordValid k x.length s Q T fs ↔
      ∃ (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T), c.InWindow s ∧ cfgRecord s c τ = fs := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, c, τ, hy, hc, rfl⟩
    let d : Cfg k Bool Q x :=
      { state := c.state
        inputPos := ⟨c.inputPos.val, by simpa only [hy] using c.inputPos.isLt⟩
        workTapes := c.workTapes
        workTapePos := c.workTapePos
        output := c.output }
    refine ⟨d, τ, hc, ?_⟩
    simp only [cfgRecord, d, hy]
  · rintro ⟨c, τ, hc, hrec⟩
    exact ⟨x, c, τ, rfl, hc, hrec⟩

/-! ### The record template -/

/-- **The record template** (design §12.8b). Two fields over the record
alphabet: the bound `n + 1` in `posWidth n` digits, which also gives the
position width, and the window of a blank tape with its head at cell `0`:
`2s + 1` blank cells with the mark at the center. The validity and enumeration
rows read the widths and the position bound off it; its window field is the
tape field of the initial record (`Turing.cfgRecord_init`). -/
def recordTemplate (Q T : Type) (n s : ℕ) : List (List (RecSym Q T)) :=
  [(binDigits (posWidth n) (n + 1)).map RecSym.digit,
    (List.range (2 * s + 1)).map fun j => RecSym.cell none (decide (j = s))]

/-- **The template's length** (design §12.8b).

**Proof sketch.** Two fields of lengths `posWidth n` and `2s + 1`, and one
separator. -/
theorem joinFields_recordTemplate_length (Q T : Type) (n s : ℕ) :
    (joinFields (recordTemplate Q T n s)).length = posWidth n + 2 * s + 2 := by
  rw [joinFields_length _ (by simp [recordTemplate])]
  simp [recordTemplate, binDigits]
  omega

/-- **The template's bound field is `Nat.bits (n + 1)`** (design §12.8b). The
position width is the bit length of `n + 1`, so the fixed-width digits of
`n + 1` are its canonical binary word. A machine obtains the bound field from
`Turing.exists_inputLengthTM`'s `Nat.bits n` by one more increment.

**Proof sketch.** `binDigits w v` lists `v.testBit j` for `j < w`, and
`Nat.bits v` lists the same bits up to the bit length of `v`, which is
`posWidth n` at `v = n + 1`. -/
theorem binDigits_posWidth_succ (n : ℕ) :
    binDigits (posWidth n) (n + 1) = Nat.bits (n + 1) := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp [binDigits, posWidth]
  · intro j hj₁ hj₂
    simp only [binDigits, List.getElem_map, List.getElem_range]
    exact (Nat.testBit_eq_inth (n + 1) j).trans (List.getI_eq_getElem _ hj₂)

/-! ### Tables -/

/-- **The fields of a table** (design §12.8b, decision 2): the header `h`
followed by the fields of the entries `es` in order. -/
def tableFields {Γ : Type*} (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) : List (List Γ) :=
  h :: es.flatten

/-- **Entry offsets** (design §12.8b): the cell, relative to the table's origin,
at which entry `j` of the table starts. At `j = |es|` it is where a further
entry would start, two cells after the last field
(`Turing.tableOffset_length`). -/
def tableOffset {Γ : Type*} (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) (j : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  fieldOffset (tableFields h es) (1 + ((es.take j).map List.length).sum)

/-- **Well-formed tables** (design §12.8b): a nonempty header, and entries of
`m` fields each, every field nonempty. Under it two consecutive blanks occur
only at the table's ends, so the seek rows apply, and entries are found by
counting fields. -/
def TableWF {Γ : Type*} (m : ℕ) (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) : Prop :=
  h ≠ [] ∧ ∀ e ∈ es, e.length = m ∧ ∀ u ∈ e, u ≠ []

/-- **A table on a tape** (design §12.8b, decision 2): tape `r` holds the field
layout of the table with header `h` and entries `es` from the origin `o`, with
two blank cells before the header and two after the last field. The cells
beyond the sentinels are arbitrary; the head may be anywhere. -/
def TableAt {K : ℕ} {Γ S : Type*} {x : List Γ} (d : Cfg K Γ S x) (r : Fin K) (o : ℤ)
    (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℤ, -2 ≤ p → p ≤ ((joinFields (tableFields h es)).length : ℤ) + 1 →
    d.workTapes r (o + p) = fieldsTape (tableFields h es) p

/-- **Table fields are nonempty** (design §12.8b): the precondition of the seek
rows, from well-formedness.

**Proof sketch.** A field of the table is the header or a field of an entry. -/
theorem TableWF.field_ne_nil {Γ : Type*} {m : ℕ} {h : List Γ} {es : List (List (List Γ))}
    (hwf : TableWF m h es) : ∀ u ∈ tableFields h es, u ≠ [] := by
  intro u hu
  rcases List.mem_cons.mp hu with rfl | hu
  · exact hwf.1
  · obtain ⟨en, hen, hu⟩ := List.mem_flatten.mp hu
    exact (hwf.2 en hen).2 u hu

/-- **Entry offsets in closed form** (design §12.8b). When no entry is empty,
entry `j` starts after the header and its separator and, for each earlier
entry, its layout and one separator.

**Proof sketch.** Split `Turing.fieldOffset` over the header and the flattened
entries, and use `Turing.fieldOffset_length` on each earlier entry. -/
theorem tableOffset_eq {Γ : Type*} (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ)))
    (hes : ∀ e ∈ es, e ≠ []) (j : ℕ) :
    tableOffset h es j =
      h.length + 1 + ((es.take j).map fun e => (joinFields e).length + 1).sum := by
  unfold tableOffset tableFields
  rw [Nat.add_comm 1, fieldOffset_cons_succ]
  congr 1
  unfold fieldOffset
  rw [show (es.take j).map List.length = (es.map List.length).take j from List.map_take,
    List.take_sum_flatten, List.map_flatten, List.sum_flatten, List.map_map]
  apply congrArg List.sum
  apply List.map_congr_left
  intro en hen
  exact (by
    simpa only [fieldOffset, List.take_length] using
      fieldOffset_length en (hes en (List.mem_of_mem_take hen)))

/-- **The end of a table** (design §12.8b). The offset past the last entry is
the table's layout length plus one: the second trailing blank, where
`Turing.seekEndTM` stops from the origin.

**Proof sketch.** At `j = |es|` the field index is `|tableFields h es|`; apply
`Turing.fieldOffset_length`, the field list being nonempty. -/
theorem tableOffset_length {Γ : Type*} (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) :
    tableOffset h es es.length = (joinFields (tableFields h es)).length + 1 := by
  unfold tableOffset
  rw [List.take_length, ← List.length_flatten]
  simpa only [tableFields, List.length_cons, Nat.add_comm] using
    fieldOffset_length (tableFields h es) (List.cons_ne_nil _ _)

/-- Every cell of a nonempty layout, including its two delimiters, lies in a
field's framed interval.

**Proof sketch.** Choose the first field whose end is at or beyond the cell. The last
field supplies existence by the public end-offset formula. Minimality and the public
successor-offset formula give the lower bound. This uses no second layout induction. -/
private theorem rt_field_cover {Γ : Type*} (fs : List (List Γ)) (hne : fs ≠ [])
    (p : ℤ) (hp : -1 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≤ ((joinFields fs).length : ℤ)) :
    ∃ (j : ℕ) (hj : j < fs.length),
      -1 ≤ p - fieldOffset fs j ∧ p - fieldOffset fs j ≤ (fs[j].length : ℤ) := by
  have hlen : 0 < fs.length := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hne
  have hlast : fs.length - 1 < fs.length := by omega
  have hend := fieldOffset_succ fs (fs.length - 1) hlast
  rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel hlen, fieldOffset_length fs hne] at hend
  have hex : ∃ (j : ℕ) (hj : j < fs.length),
      p ≤ (fieldOffset fs j : ℤ) + (fs[j].length : ℤ) := by
    exact ⟨fs.length - 1, hlast, by omega⟩
  obtain ⟨hj, hu⟩ := Nat.find_spec hex
  refine ⟨Nat.find hex, hj, ?_, by omega⟩
  by_cases hz : Nat.find hex = 0
  · simpa only [hz, fieldOffset, List.take_zero, List.map_nil, List.sum_nil,
      Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero] using hp
  · have hprev : Nat.find hex - 1 < fs.length := by omega
    have hmin := Nat.find_min hex (show Nat.find hex - 1 < Nat.find hex by omega)
    have hnot : ¬p ≤ (fieldOffset fs (Nat.find hex - 1) : ℤ) +
        (fs[Nat.find hex - 1].length : ℤ) := fun h => hmin ⟨hprev, h⟩
    have hstep := fieldOffset_succ fs (Nat.find hex - 1) hprev
    rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel (show 1 ≤ Nat.find hex by omega)] at hstep
    omega

/-- A nonempty contiguous block of fields has the same framed cells inside a
larger layout, and its interval is contained in that layout.

**Proof sketch.** Splitting a list prefix adds field offsets. Locate each requested
cell in one field using `rt_field_cover`, and apply `fieldsTape_field` twice.
The last field and `fieldOffset_add_length_le` give containment. -/
private theorem rt_fields_slice {Γ : Type*} (pre gs post : List (List Γ))
    (hne : gs ≠ []) :
    fieldOffset (pre ++ (gs ++ post)) pre.length + (joinFields gs).length ≤
        (joinFields (pre ++ (gs ++ post))).length ∧
    ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ ((joinFields gs).length : ℤ) →
      fieldsTape (pre ++ (gs ++ post))
        ((fieldOffset (pre ++ (gs ++ post)) pre.length : ℤ) + p) = fieldsTape gs p := by
  let fs := pre ++ (gs ++ post)
  have hidx (j : ℕ) (hj : j < gs.length) : pre.length + j < fs.length := by
    simp only [fs, List.length_append]
    omega
  have hfield (j : ℕ) (hj : j < gs.length) :
      fs[pre.length + j]'(hidx j hj) = gs[j] := by
    simp [fs, List.getElem_append_right, List.getElem_append_left, hj]
  have hoff (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ gs.length) :
      fieldOffset fs (pre.length + j) = fieldOffset fs pre.length + fieldOffset gs j := by
    simp only [fs, fieldOffset, List.take_length_add_append,
      List.take_append_of_le_length hj, List.map_append, List.sum_append, List.take_left]
  have hlen : 0 < gs.length := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hne
  have hlast : gs.length - 1 < gs.length := by omega
  have hspan := fieldOffset_add_length_le fs (pre.length + (gs.length - 1))
    (hidx _ hlast)
  rw [hfield _ hlast, hoff _ (by omega)] at hspan
  have hend := fieldOffset_succ gs (gs.length - 1) hlast
  rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel hlen, fieldOffset_length gs hne] at hend
  refine ⟨show fieldOffset fs pre.length + (joinFields gs).length ≤
    (joinFields fs).length from by omega, ?_⟩
  intro p hp hp'
  obtain ⟨j, hj, hlo, hhi⟩ := rt_field_cover gs hne p hp hp'
  have hbig := fieldsTape_field fs (pre.length + j) (hidx j hj)
    (p - fieldOffset gs j) hlo (by simpa only [hfield j hj] using hhi)
  have hsmall := fieldsTape_field gs j hj (p - fieldOffset gs j) hlo hhi
  have ho := hoff j (by omega)
  have heq : (fieldOffset fs (pre.length + j) : ℤ) + (p - fieldOffset gs j) =
      (fieldOffset fs pre.length : ℤ) + p := by omega
  rw [heq, hfield j hj] at hbig
  rw [show (fieldOffset gs j : ℤ) + (p - fieldOffset gs j) = p by omega] at hsmall
  exact hbig.trans hsmall.symm

/-- **An entry of a table is a record at its offset** (design §12.8b). If a
well-formed table sits at `o` on tape `r` and the head is at entry `j`'s offset,
then the first `m₀ > 0` fields of entry `j` form a record at the head in the
sense of `Turing.RecordAt`. At `m₀ = m` this is the whole entry; at `m₀ = k + 3`
inside an entry of a record and a flag field, it is the record.

**Proof sketch.** `Turing.fieldsTape_field` on the table's field list, at the
field indices of entry `j`. The cell before the entry is the separator after
the header or after the previous entry, and the cell after the `m₀` fields is
the separator after field `m₀ - 1`, or the first trailing blank. -/
theorem TableAt.recordAt_take {K : ℕ} {Γ S : Type*} {x : List Γ} {d : Cfg K Γ S x}
    {r : Fin K} {o : ℤ} {m : ℕ} {h : List Γ} {es : List (List (List Γ))}
    (ht : TableAt d r o h es) (hwf : TableWF m h es) (j : ℕ) (hj : j < es.length)
    (hpos : d.workTapePos r = o + tableOffset h es j) (m₀ : ℕ) (hm₀ : 0 < m₀)
    (hm₀m : m₀ ≤ m) : RecordAt d r (es[j].take m₀) := by
  let pre := h :: (es.take j).flatten
  let gs := es[j].take m₀
  let post := es[j].drop m₀ ++ (es.drop (j + 1)).flatten
  have hem : es[j].length = m := (hwf.2 es[j] (List.getElem_mem hj)).1
  have hgs : gs ≠ [] := by
    apply List.ne_nil_of_length_pos
    simp only [gs, List.length_take, hem, Nat.min_eq_left hm₀m]
    exact hm₀
  have hes := (List.take_append_drop j es).symm
  rw [List.drop_eq_getElem_cons hj] at hes
  have hlayout : tableFields h es = pre ++ (gs ++ post) := by
    calc
      tableFields h es = h :: ((es.take j).flatten ++
          (es[j] ++ (es.drop (j + 1)).flatten)) := by
        unfold tableFields
        conv_lhs => rw [hes]
        simp only [List.flatten_append, List.flatten_cons]
      _ = pre ++ (gs ++ post) := by
        simp only [pre, gs, post, List.cons_append, ← List.append_assoc,
          List.take_append_drop]
  have hoff : fieldOffset (tableFields h es) pre.length = tableOffset h es j := by
    simp only [tableOffset, pre, List.length_cons, List.length_flatten, Nat.add_comm]
  have hslice := rt_fields_slice pre gs post hgs
  rw [← hlayout, hoff] at hslice
  intro p hp hp'
  rw [hpos, add_assoc, ht ((tableOffset h es j : ℤ) + p) (by omega) (by
    have := hslice.1
    change p ≤ ((joinFields gs).length : ℤ) at hp'
    omega)]
  exact hslice.2 p hp hp'

/-! ### The end-to-start adapter -/

/-- **The end-to-start adapter** (design §12.8b, decision 2 of §12.8a §9):
from the cell where `Turing.seekEndTM` stops, the second blank after a field
layout, skip back over the last field (`Turing.skipBackTM`), then seek the
start (`Turing.seekStartTM`). The two are joined by one seam. Nothing is
written. -/
def tableRewindTM {Γ : Type*} (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : MultiTapeTM k Γ (SeekPhase ⊕ SeekPhase) :=
  seamCompTM (skipBackTM k i) .done (seekStartTM k i) .run

/-- **The end-to-start adapter, framed** (design §12.8b). Let tape `i` hold a
nonempty list `ws` of nonempty fields in the field layout, preceded by two
blank cells and followed by one, with the head on the cell after that blank,
at `D = fieldOffset ws |ws|` from the layout's start. Then the adapter reaches
`Sum.inr done` at exactly `D + 7`, with the head of tape `i` at the layout's
start and nothing else changed, and not earlier. The current cell and the cells
beyond the sentinels are arbitrary. Up to the exit the head stays within
`[pos - D - 2, pos]`, and every other head is fixed. For a table at `o`, `ws`
is its field list, the start is `o`, and `D + 7` is the layout length plus
eight.

**Proof sketch.** `Turing.seamCompTM_run_ofCfg` with `Turing.skipBackTM_run_ofCfg`
over the last field `u`, which starts at `pos - |u| - 1`, in `|u| + 3` steps,
then the dispatch step, then `Turing.seekStartTM_run_ofCfg` from the first cell
of `u`, which is nonblank, over the remaining fields, in `D' + 4` steps with
`D = D' + |u| + 1`. The framing of `u` and of the remaining fields is
`Turing.fieldsTape_field` and the split of `Turing.fieldOffset` at the last
field. The first-return cut is `Turing.seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg`.

**Fill appendix.** The two phase contracts supply the exact run and cut.
`Turing.seamCompTM_visitedByTapeHead_ofCfg` transports their head bounds;
`rt_fields_slice` restricts the original frame to the prefix before the last field. -/
theorem tableRewindTM_run_ofCfg {Γ : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Γ} (i : Fin k)
    (ws : List (List Γ)) (hne : ws ≠ []) (hws : ∀ u ∈ ws, u ≠ [])
    (d : Cfg k Γ (SeekPhase ⊕ SeekPhase) x) (hstate : d.state = some (Sum.inl .run))
    (hw : ∀ p : ℤ, -2 ≤ p → p < (fieldOffset ws ws.length : ℤ) →
      d.workTapes i (d.workTapePos i - fieldOffset ws ws.length + p) = fieldsTape ws p) :
    (tableRewindTM k i).runFrom d (fieldOffset ws ws.length + 7) =
        { d with
          state := some (Sum.inr .done)
          workTapePos := Function.update d.workTapePos i
            (d.workTapePos i - fieldOffset ws ws.length) } ∧
      (∀ t < fieldOffset ws ws.length + 7,
        ((tableRewindTM k i).runFrom d t).state ≠ some (Sum.inr .done)) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ fieldOffset ws ws.length + 7 →
        if j = i then
          ((tableRewindTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - fieldOffset ws ws.length - 2) (d.workTapePos j)
        else ((tableRewindTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
  classical
  have hlen : 0 < ws.length := List.length_pos_iff.mpr hne
  let a := ws.length - 1
  have ha : a < ws.length := by omega
  let pre := ws.take a
  let u := ws[a]
  have hprelen : pre.length = a := by simp [pre, Nat.min_eq_left (Nat.le_of_lt ha)]
  have hsplit : ws = pre ++ [u] := by
    simpa only [pre, u, show a + 1 = ws.length by omega, List.take_length] using
      (List.take_append_getElem ha).symm
  have ho : fieldOffset ws a = fieldOffset pre pre.length := by
    rw [hprelen]
    simp only [fieldOffset, pre, List.take_take, Nat.min_self]
  have hD : fieldOffset ws ws.length = fieldOffset pre pre.length + u.length + 1 := by
    have hh := fieldOffset_succ ws a ha
    rw [show a + 1 = ws.length by omega, ho] at hh
    simpa only [u, Nat.add_assoc] using hh
  let c₀ : Cfg k Γ SeekPhase x := d.mapState (fun _ => .run)
  let c₁ : Cfg k Γ SeekPhase x :=
    { c₀ with
      state := some .done
      workTapePos := Function.update c₀.workTapePos i (c₀.workTapePos i - u.length - 1) }
  have hc₀ : c₀.state = some .run := by simp [c₀, Cfg.mapState, hstate]
  have hentry : c₀.mapState Sum.inl = d := by
    apply Cfg.ext <;> simp [c₀, Cfg.mapState, hstate]
  have hu (p : ℤ) (hp : -1 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≤ (u.length : ℤ)) :
      c₀.workTapes i (c₀.workTapePos i - u.length - 1 + p) = FinTM.bufferTape u p := by
    change d.workTapes i (d.workTapePos i - u.length - 1 + p) = _
    have heq : d.workTapePos i - u.length - 1 + p =
        d.workTapePos i - fieldOffset ws ws.length + ((fieldOffset ws a : ℤ) + p) := by
      rw [ho]
      omega
    rw [heq, hw _ (by omega) (by rw [ho]; omega)]
    exact fieldsTape_field ws a ha p hp hp'
  obtain ⟨h₁, hcut₁, hrad₁⟩ := skipBackTM_run_ofCfg i u c₀ hc₀ hu
  change (skipBackTM k i).runFrom c₀ (u.length + 3) = c₁ at h₁
  let c₂ := c₁.mapState (fun _ => SeekPhase.run)
  have hnonempty : u ≠ [] := hws u (List.getElem_mem ha)
  have hcur : c₂.workTapes i (c₂.workTapePos i) ≠ none := by
    have hh := hu 0 (by omega) (by omega)
    simp only [add_zero, c₀, Cfg.mapState] at hh
    change d.workTapes i (Function.update d.workTapePos i
      (d.workTapePos i - u.length - 1) i) ≠ none
    rw [Function.update_self, hh]
    cases he : u with
    | nil => exact False.elim (hnonempty he)
    | cons b bs => simp [FinTM.bufferTape]
  have hframe (p : ℤ) (hp : -2 ≤ p)
      (hp' : p < (fieldOffset pre pre.length : ℤ)) :
      c₂.workTapes i (c₂.workTapePos i - fieldOffset pre pre.length + p) =
        fieldsTape pre p := by
    change d.workTapes i (Function.update d.workTapePos i
      (d.workTapePos i - u.length - 1) i - fieldOffset pre pre.length + p) = _
    rw [Function.update_self]
    have heq : d.workTapePos i - u.length - 1 - fieldOffset pre pre.length + p =
        d.workTapePos i - fieldOffset ws ws.length + p := by omega
    rw [heq, hw p hp (by omega)]
    by_cases hp0 : 0 ≤ p
    · have hprene : pre ≠ [] := by
        intro he
        simp [he, fieldOffset] at hp'
        omega
      have hs := (rt_fields_slice [] pre [u] hprene).2 p (by omega) (by
        have := fieldOffset_length pre hprene
        omega)
      simpa only [List.nil_append, fieldOffset, List.length_nil, List.take_zero, List.map_nil,
        List.sum_nil, Nat.cast_zero, zero_add, ← hsplit] using hs
    · simp [fieldsTape, hp0]
  have hpre : ∀ v ∈ pre, v ≠ [] := fun v hv => hws v (List.mem_of_mem_take hv)
  obtain ⟨h₂, hcut₂, hrad₂⟩ := seekStartTM_run_ofCfg i pre hpre c₂ rfl hcur hframe
  let c₃ : Cfg k Γ SeekPhase x :=
    { c₂ with
      state := some .done
      workTapePos := Function.update c₂.workTapePos i
        (c₂.workTapePos i - fieldOffset pre pre.length) }
  change (seekStartTM k i).runFrom (c₁.mapState fun _ => SeekPhase.run)
    (fieldOffset pre pre.length + 4) = c₃ at h₂
  have htime : u.length + 3 + 1 + (fieldOffset pre pre.length + 4) =
      fieldOffset ws ws.length + 7 := by omega
  have hrun := seamCompTM_run_ofCfg (skipBackTM k i) .done (seekStartTM k i) .run
    h₁ rfl hcut₁ h₂
  have hcut := seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg (skipBackTM k i) .done
    (seekStartTM k i) .run .done h₁ rfl hcut₁ h₂ rfl hcut₂
  rw [hentry, htime] at hrun hcut
  refine ⟨?_, hcut, ?_⟩
  · change (tableRewindTM k i).runFrom d (fieldOffset ws ws.length + 7) =
      c₃.mapState Sum.inr at hrun
    rw [hrun]
    apply Cfg.ext <;> simp [c₃, c₂, c₁, c₀, Cfg.mapState, Function.update_idem,
      show d.workTapePos i - (u.length : ℤ) - 1 - fieldOffset pre pre.length =
        d.workTapePos i - fieldOffset ws ws.length by omega]
  · intro j t ht
    let region := Finset.Icc
      (if j = i then d.workTapePos j - fieldOffset ws ws.length - 2 else d.workTapePos j)
      (d.workTapePos j)
    have cover :
        (skipBackTM k i).visitedByTapeHead c₀ (u.length + 3) j ∪
          (seekStartTM k i).visitedByTapeHead c₂ (fieldOffset pre pre.length + 4) j ⊆
        region := by
      apply Finset.union_subset
      · apply Finset.image_subset_iff.mpr
        intro v hv
        have bounds := hrad₁ j v (Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hv))
        by_cases hji : j = i
        · subst j
          simp only [if_true, Finset.mem_Icc] at bounds
          change d.workTapePos i - (u.length : ℤ) - 2 ≤ _ ∧ _ ≤ d.workTapePos i at bounds
          simp only [region, if_true, Finset.mem_Icc]
          omega
        · simp only [if_neg hji] at bounds
          simp only [region, if_neg hji, Finset.mem_Icc]
          rw [bounds]
          simp only [c₀, Cfg.mapState, le_refl, and_self]
      · apply Finset.image_subset_iff.mpr
        intro v hv
        have bounds := hrad₂ j v (Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hv))
        by_cases hji : j = i
        · subst j
          simp only [if_true, Finset.mem_Icc] at bounds
          change Function.update d.workTapePos i (d.workTapePos i - u.length - 1) i -
              fieldOffset pre pre.length - 2 ≤ _ ∧
            _ ≤ Function.update d.workTapePos i (d.workTapePos i - u.length - 1) i at bounds
          rw [Function.update_self] at bounds
          simp only [region, if_true, Finset.mem_Icc]
          omega
        · simp only [if_neg hji] at bounds
          simp only [region, if_neg hji, Finset.mem_Icc]
          rw [bounds]
          simp only [c₂, c₁, c₀, Cfg.mapState, Function.update_of_ne hji, le_refl, and_self]
    have transfer := seamCompTM_visitedByTapeHead_ofCfg (skipBackTM k i) .done
      (seekStartTM k i) .run (T₂ := fieldOffset pre pre.length + 4) h₁ rfl hcut₁ j
    rw [hentry, htime] at transfer
    have membership : ((tableRewindTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈ region := by
      apply cover
      apply transfer
      exact Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ (Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.lt_succ_of_le ht))
    by_cases hji : j = i
    · simpa only [region, if_pos hji] using membership
    · simp only [region, if_neg hji, Finset.mem_Icc] at membership
      simpa only [if_neg hji] using le_antisymm membership.2 membership.1

/-! ### Copying a field list -/

/-- The fixed field count determines a finite sum of the catalog phase types. -/
private def rt_copyState : ℕ → Type
  | 0 => Unit
  | 1 => SweepPhase
  | m + 2 => SweepPhase ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕
      (rt_copyState (m + 1) ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕ SeekPhase))))

/-- The recursive field-copy controller has finitely many states. -/
private instance rt_copyState_fintype : (m : ℕ) → Fintype (rt_copyState m)
  | 0 => inferInstanceAs (Fintype Unit)
  | 1 => inferInstanceAs (Fintype SweepPhase)
  | m + 2 => by
    letI := rt_copyState_fintype (m + 1)
    change Fintype (SweepPhase ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕
      (rt_copyState (m + 1) ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕ SeekPhase)))))
    infer_instance

/-- Equality of the finite field-copy control states is decidable. -/
private instance rt_copyState_decidableEq : (m : ℕ) → DecidableEq (rt_copyState m)
  | 0 => inferInstanceAs (DecidableEq Unit)
  | 1 => inferInstanceAs (DecidableEq SweepPhase)
  | m + 2 => by
    letI := rt_copyState_decidableEq (m + 1)
    change DecidableEq (SweepPhase ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕
      (rt_copyState (m + 1) ⊕ (SeekPhase ⊕ SeekPhase)))))
    infer_instance

/-- The field-copy entry is the first copy's sweep state; the empty case is a no-op. -/
private def rt_copyEntry : (m : ℕ) → rt_copyState m
  | 0 => ()
  | 1 => .sweep
  | _ + 2 => .inl .sweep

/-- The field-copy exit is the last backward skip's anchor. -/
