import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Encoding

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Universal machine: startup infrastructure

Prefix-local startup layer of the universal machine: parsing the doubled-bit
code region of `pairEncode α x`, running the scheme's canonizer on the
extracted code, embedding the virtual input head into the paired input's
verbatim `x` region, and capturing the canonical table on a dedicated work
tape before control transfers to the table interpreter. This file was split
out mechanically from `Universal.lean` at the epoch-3→4 merge; its contents
are the epoch-3 fill, batches B (WIP) and B2 (completion), unchanged.

## Main definitions / Main results

* `Turing.universalCanonTM` — prefix extraction composed with the scheme's canonizer.
* `Turing.universalCaptureTM` — output capture onto a table tape, then transfer
  to a four-tape interpreter.
* `Turing.universalCanon_complete` — the canonical serialization is produced at
  a suffix-independent time.
* `Turing.universalCapture_start` — every completed source computation reaches
  the interpreter with the table captured.
* `Turing.universalInput_read` / `Turing.universalInput_move` — virtual
  input-head emulation over the verbatim `x` region.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.4.1, Theorem 1.9, pp. 20-21.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-! ### Private prefix-local startup infrastructure

Implementation notes (epoch 3B). The extraction machine stops immediately after
reading the aligned separator. Buffered composition then serves the canonizer's
input from the extracted word and keeps the physical suffix head stationary.

**Incomplete implementation (epoch 3B).** The startup, virtual-boundary lemmas,
and conditional block-simulation assembly below are proved. The live-source
serialized-table block obligation in `universal` remains admitted. The concrete
interpreter is a candidate, not a completed proof of the headline theorem.

**Completion (epoch 3B2).** The preceding paragraph records the delivered WIP.
The live serialized-table block is now proved below, including exact phase costs,
record selection, action application, and the original code-only block bound.
The controller and all startup and assembly constructions are unchanged.
-/

open FinTM

/-- Doubling the code and appending its delimiter has suffix-independent length. -/
lemma universal_pair_length (α x : List Bool) :
    (pairEncode α x).length = 2 * α.length + 2 + x.length := by
  induction α with
  | nil => simp [pairEncode]; omega
  | cons b α ih =>
    simp only [pairEncode, List.flatMap_cons, List.cons_append, List.nil_append,
      List.length_cons] at *
    omega

/-- Both cells of a doubled code bit are read before the separator. -/
private lemma universal_pair_get (α x : List Bool) (j : ℕ) (hj : j < α.length) :
    (pairEncode α x)[2 * j]? = some α[j] ∧
      (pairEncode α x)[2 * j + 1]? = some α[j] := by
  induction α generalizing j with
  | nil => simp at hj
  | cons b α ih =>
    cases j with
    | zero => simp [pairEncode]
    | succ j =>
      have h := ih j (by simpa using hj)
      simpa only [pairEncode, List.flatMap_cons, List.cons_append,
        List.nil_append, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one, Nat.add_assoc,
        List.getElem?_cons_succ, List.getElem_cons_succ] using h

/-- The delimiter begins immediately after the doubled code. -/
private lemma universal_pair_separator (α x : List Bool) :
    (pairEncode α x)[2 * α.length]? = some false ∧
      (pairEncode α x)[2 * α.length + 1]? = some true := by
  induction α with
  | nil => simp [pairEncode]
  | cons b α ih =>
    simpa only [pairEncode, List.flatMap_cons, List.cons_append,
      List.nil_append, List.length_cons, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one, Nat.add_assoc,
      List.getElem?_cons_succ] using ih

/-- Two-state-register parser. The outer optional state of a configuration is
halting; `none` inside the finite control means that the first half of a pair is
next. On a valid pair, the second half emits its undoubled bit; on the separator
it moves to the suffix and halts without emitting. -/
private def universalPrefixTM : FinTM Bool where
  k := 0
  State := Option Bool
  tm :=
    { q₀ := none
      tr := fun q inp _ => match q with
        | none => ⟨.pos, fun i => i.elim0, none, inp.map some⟩
        | some b =>
          if inp = some b then
            ⟨.pos, fun i => i.elim0, some b, some none⟩
          else
            ⟨.pos, fun i => i.elim0, none, none⟩ }

/-- The prefix parser carries no work tapes. -/
private def universalPrefixCfg (α x : List Bool) (q : Option (Option Bool))
    (p : Fin ((pairEncode α x).length + 2)) (out : List Bool) :
    Cfg 0 Bool (Option Bool) (pairEncode α x) :=
  ⟨q, p, fun i => i.elim0, fun i => i.elim0, out⟩

/-- A single parser transition, with its input read supplied explicitly. -/
private lemma universalPrefix_step (α x : List Bool) (q : Option Bool)
    (p : Fin ((pairEncode α x).length + 2)) (out : List Bool) (b : Option Bool)
    (hb : (universalPrefixCfg α x (some q) p out).inputSymbol = b) :
    universalPrefixTM.tm.step (universalPrefixCfg α x (some q) p out) =
      let a := universalPrefixTM.tm.tr q b (fun i => i.elim0)
      universalPrefixCfg α x a.state (moveInputPos p a.inputTape)
        (out ++ a.output.toList) := by
  change (universalPrefixTM.tm.tr q
    (universalPrefixCfg α x (some q) p out).inputSymbol
    (universalPrefixCfg α x (some q) p out).workTapeSymbols).apply _ = _
  rw [hb]
  exact Cfg.ext_zero_tapes rfl rfl rfl

/-- After `2j` steps exactly `j` code bits have been consumed and emitted.

**Proof sketch.** The aligned cells at offsets `2j` and `2j+1` contain the same
code bit. The first transition remembers it, and the second emits it. Neither
transition can reach the suffix, and the work-tape fields are vacuous. -/
private lemma universalPrefix_bits (α x : List Bool) : ∀ j, (hj : j ≤ α.length) →
    universalPrefixTM.tm.runFrom (universalPrefixTM.tm.initCfg (pairEncode α x))
      (2 * j) =
    universalPrefixCfg α x (some none)
      ⟨2 * j + 1, by rw [universal_pair_length]; omega⟩ (α.take j) := by
  intro j
  induction j with
  | zero =>
    intro _
    apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes <;> rfl
  | succ j ih =>
    intro hj
    have hl := universal_pair_length α x
    have hg := universal_pair_get α x j (by omega)
    conv_lhs => rw [show 2 * (j + 1) = 2 * j + 1 + 1 by omega]
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step',
      ih (by omega)]
    rw [universalPrefix_step _ _ _ _ _ (some α[j]) (by
      rw [inputSymbol_at _ (2 * j) (by omega) (by rfl)]; exact hg.1)]
    simp only [universalPrefixTM, Option.map_some, Option.toList_none, List.append_nil]
    rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega)]
    rw [universalPrefix_step _ _ _ _ _ (some α[j]) (by
      rw [inputSymbol_at _ (2 * j + 1) (by omega) (by rfl)]; exact hg.2)]
    simp only [universalPrefixTM, ↓reduceIte, Option.toList_some]
    rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega)]
    apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes
    · rfl
    · apply Fin.ext; simp only [universalPrefixCfg, Fin.val_mk]; omega
    · rw [List.take_succ, List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by omega)]
      rfl

/-- Prefix-only extraction takes exactly `2|α|+2` steps, emits `α`, and parks
at `2|α|+3`. This includes empty code and empty suffix; no suffix cell is read.

**Proof sketch.** Apply the doubled-prefix induction to the whole code, then
execute the two separator transitions. The last transition moves onto, but does
not read, the suffix's first cell (the right blank when the suffix is empty). -/
private lemma universalPrefix_start (α x : List Bool) :
    universalPrefixTM.tm.runFrom (universalPrefixTM.tm.initCfg (pairEncode α x))
      (2 * α.length + 2) =
    universalPrefixCfg α x none
      ⟨2 * α.length + 3, by rw [universal_pair_length]; omega⟩ α := by
  have hl := universal_pair_length α x
  have hg := universal_pair_separator α x
  conv_lhs => rw [show 2 * α.length + 2 = 2 * α.length + 1 + 1 by omega]
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step',
    universalPrefix_bits α x α.length (le_refl _), List.take_length]
  rw [universalPrefix_step _ _ _ _ _ (some false) (by
    rw [inputSymbol_at _ (2 * α.length) (by omega) (by rfl)]; exact hg.1)]
  simp only [universalPrefixTM, Option.map_some, Option.toList_none, List.append_nil]
  rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega)]
  rw [universalPrefix_step _ _ _ _ _ (some true) (by
    rw [inputSymbol_at _ (2 * α.length + 1) (by omega) (by rfl)]; exact hg.2)]
  simp only [universalPrefixTM, Bool.true_eq_false, Option.some.injEq, ↓reduceIte,
    Option.toList_none, List.append_nil]
  apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes
  · rfl
  · rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega)]
  · rfl



/-- One transition remains after the doubled code and the delimiter's first bit. -/
private lemma universalPrefix_penultimate (α x : List Bool) :
    universalPrefixTM.tm.runFrom (universalPrefixTM.tm.initCfg (pairEncode α x))
      (2 * α.length + 1) =
    universalPrefixCfg α x (some (some false))
      ⟨2 * α.length + 2, by rw [universal_pair_length]; omega⟩ α := by
  have hl := universal_pair_length α x
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step',
    universalPrefix_bits α x α.length (le_refl _), List.take_length]
  rw [universalPrefix_step _ _ _ _ _ (some false) (by
    rw [inputSymbol_at _ (2 * α.length) (by omega) (by rfl)]
    exact (universal_pair_separator α x).1)]
  simp only [universalPrefixTM, Option.map_some, Option.toList_none, List.append_nil]
  rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega)]

/-- A live later configuration excludes all earlier halts, since halting is
absorbing. This is used for administrative phases, independently of outputs. -/
private lemma universal_live_before {k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (tm : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) {s t : ℕ}
    (hst : s ≤ t) (ht : (tm.runFrom cfg t).state ≠ none) :
    (tm.runFrom cfg s).state ≠ none := by
  intro hs
  obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hst
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt _ hs] at ht
  exact ht hs

/-- No prefix extraction step before the separator's second bit can halt. -/
private lemma universalPrefix_live (α x : List Bool) (s : ℕ)
    (hs : s < 2 * α.length + 2) :
    (universalPrefixTM.tm.runFrom
      (universalPrefixTM.tm.initCfg (pairEncode α x)) s).state ≠ none := by
  apply universal_live_before universalPrefixTM.tm _ (show s ≤ 2 * α.length + 1 by omega)
  rw [universalPrefix_penultimate]
  exact Option.some_ne_none _

/-- Extract the code prefix, then run the given canonizer on the code buffer. -/
def universalCanonTM (c : EffectiveMachineCode) : FinTM Bool :=
  bufferedCompTM universalPrefixTM c.canonizer

/-- Exact prefix-local canonizer start: `3|α|+4` transitions suffice, regardless
of the suffix, and its first symbol has not been read.

**Proof sketch.** Extraction takes `2|α|+2` transitions and is live until its
last transition. The existing buffered first-phase invariant captures precisely
`α`. Its unconditional first left move and rewind use `|α|+2` further transitions,
including when `α` is empty. The resulting second-phase configuration starts the
canonizer on virtual input `α`, while the real head remains at the suffix start. -/
private lemma universalCanon_start (c : EffectiveMachineCode) (α x : List Bool) :
    (universalCanonTM c).tm.runFrom
      ((universalCanonTM c).tm.initCfg (pairEncode α x)) (3 * α.length + 4) =
    bufferedSecondCfg universalPrefixTM c.canonizer (c.canonizer.tm.initCfg α) true
      ⟨2 * α.length + 3, by rw [universal_pair_length]; omega⟩
      (fun i => i.elim0) (fun i => i.elim0) := by
  change (bufferedCompTM universalPrefixTM c.canonizer).tm.runFrom _ _ = _
  rw [show 3 * α.length + 4 = (2 * α.length + 2) + (α.length + 2) by omega,
    MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, bufferedFirstCfg_init,
    bufferedFirstCfg_run universalPrefixTM c.canonizer _ _
      (fun s hs => universalPrefix_live α x s hs), universalPrefix_start]
  exact bufferedFirstCfg_rewind universalPrefixTM c.canonizer _ rfl

/-- The entire canonizer run serves input from the code tape and leaves the
physical suffix head fixed. Its bound depends on the code alone. -/
private lemma universalCanon_run (c : EffectiveMachineCode) (α x : List Bool) (t : ℕ) :
    ∃ b, (universalCanonTM c).tm.runFrom
      ((universalCanonTM c).tm.initCfg (pairEncode α x)) (3 * α.length + 4 + t) =
    bufferedSecondCfg universalPrefixTM c.canonizer
      (c.canonizer.tm.runFrom (c.canonizer.tm.initCfg α) t) b
      ⟨2 * α.length + 3, by rw [universal_pair_length]; omega⟩
      (fun i => i.elim0) (fun i => i.elim0) := by
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, universalCanon_start]
  obtain ⟨b, -, he⟩ := bufferedSecondCfg_run universalPrefixTM c.canonizer
    (c.canonizer.tm.initCfg α) true
    (by constructor <;> intro h <;> simp_all [VirtualTag])
    (x := pairEncode α x)
    (⟨2 * α.length + 3, by rw [universal_pair_length]; omega⟩)
    (fun i => i.elim0) (fun i => i.elim0) t
  exact ⟨b, he⟩

/-- Exact canonical-table correspondence at a suffix-independent time.
The chosen scheme is a parameter; this uses only its canonizer contract, never
`exists_effectiveMachineCode`.

**Proof sketch.** The virtual canonizer run ends with precisely the contracted
serialization. Project state, output, and input position from the complete
configuration equality. Absorbing halting permits using the supplied time bound. -/
lemma universalCanon_complete (c : EffectiveMachineCode) (α x : List Bool) :
    let cfg := (universalCanonTM c).tm.runFrom
      ((universalCanonTM c).tm.initCfg (pairEncode α x))
      (3 * α.length + 4 + c.canonizerTime α.length)
    cfg.state = none ∧ cfg.output = (c.decode α).serialize ∧
      cfg.inputPos.val = 2 * α.length + 3 := by
  dsimp only
  obtain ⟨b, he⟩ := universalCanon_run c α x (c.canonizerTime α.length)
  rw [he]
  have hc := (computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (c.canonizer_computes α)
  exact ⟨by simp only [bufferedSecondCfg, hc.1, Option.map_none], hc.2, rfl⟩


/-- Suffix lookups use the code-prefix offset and do not change the suffix. -/
private lemma universal_pair_suffix (α x : List Bool) (j : ℕ) :
    (pairEncode α x)[2 * α.length + 2 + j]? = x[j]? := by
  have hl : (α.flatMap fun b => [b, b]).length = 2 * α.length := by
    have h := universal_pair_length α []
    simp only [pairEncode, List.length_append, List.length_cons, List.length_nil] at h
    omega
  simp only [pairEncode, List.append_assoc]
  rw [List.getElem?_append_right (by omega)]
  rw [hl, show 2 * α.length + 2 + j - 2 * α.length = j + 1 + 1 by omega]
  rfl

/-- Embed a virtual suffix head, including both boundaries, into the physical
paired input. Virtual position zero lies on the delimiter's last cell. -/
def universalInputPos (α x : List Bool) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) :
    Fin ((pairEncode α x).length + 2) :=
  ⟨2 * α.length + 2 + p.val, by rw [universal_pair_length]; omega⟩

/-- Only the physical input position changes in this configuration embedding. -/
private def universalInputCfg {k : ℕ} {S : Type} (α : List Bool) {x : List Bool}
    (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) : Cfg k Bool S (pairEncode α x) :=
  ⟨cfg.state, universalInputPos α x cfg.inputPos, cfg.workTapes, cfg.workTapePos,
    cfg.output⟩

/-- A permanent marker at coordinate zero identifies exactly the virtual left
boundary. The marker tape's head follows the virtual position, not the physical
delimiter coordinate. -/
private lemma universal_marker (p : ℕ) :
    bufferTape [true] (p : ℤ) = if p = 0 then some true else none := by
  rw [bufferTape_nat]
  cases p <;> simp

/-- Masking the delimiter by the left marker yields the native input symbol,
including the adjacent left and right boundaries of an empty suffix.

**Proof sketch.** At virtual zero the explicit marker supplies blank. At every
positive virtual position, the physical lookup is the suffix lookup at position
minus one. The optional lookup formulation also covers the right blank. -/
lemma universalInput_read {k : ℕ} {S : Type} (α : List Bool) {x : List Bool}
    (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) :
    (if bufferTape [true] (cfg.inputPos.val : ℤ) = some true then none
      else (universalInputCfg α cfg).inputSymbol) = cfg.inputSymbol := by
  rw [universal_marker]
  by_cases h0 : cfg.inputPos.val = 0
  · have hp : cfg.inputPos = 0 := Fin.ext h0
    simp [hp, Cfg.inputSymbol]
  · simp only [if_neg h0, reduceCtorEq, ↓reduceIte]
    have hp := cfg.inputPos.isLt
    have hi : cfg.inputPos.val - 1 ≤ x.length := by omega
    have he : cfg.inputPos.val = (cfg.inputPos.val - 1) + 1 := by omega
    rw [inputSymbol_at cfg _ hi he]
    rw [inputSymbol_at _ (2 * α.length + 2 + (cfg.inputPos.val - 1))
      (by rw [universal_pair_length]; omega)
      (by simp only [universalInputCfg, universalInputPos, Fin.val_mk]; omega)]
    exact universal_pair_suffix α x _

/-- The marker-derived boundary tag satisfies the existing virtual-movement
contract. At the right blank the marker is absent, including on empty input. -/
private lemma universalInput_tag {n : ℕ} (p : Fin (n + 2)) :
    VirtualTag p (decide (bufferTape [true] (p.val : ℤ) ≠ some true)) := by
  rw [universal_marker]
  constructor
  · intro h; simp [h]
  · intro h; simp [h]

/-- Clamped virtual motion commutes with the physical suffix embedding, and
moving the marker head by the same amount preserves its coordinate invariant.

**Proof sketch.** The established buffer-motion lemma gives the integer equation
for the virtual head. Both its old and new positions lie in the virtual input's
closed boundary interval. Adding the prefix offset puts this whole interval
inside the physical tape, so the same clamped move realizes the shifted equation.
In particular, a left move at virtual zero is suppressed. -/
lemma universalInput_move {k : ℕ} {S : Type} (α : List Bool) {x : List Bool}
    (cfg : Cfg k Bool S x) (d : SignType) :
    let b := decide (bufferTape [true] (cfg.inputPos.val : ℤ) ≠ some true)
    let m := virtualMove b cfg.inputSymbol d
    moveInputPos (universalInputPos α x cfg.inputPos) m =
      universalInputPos α x (moveInputPos cfg.inputPos d) ∧
    (cfg.inputPos.val : ℤ) + (m : ℤ) = ((moveInputPos cfg.inputPos d).val : ℤ) := by
  dsimp only
  have hm := (virtualMove_correct cfg _ (universalInput_tag cfg.inputPos) d).1
  have hl := universal_pair_length α x
  have hn := (moveInputPos cfg.inputPos d).isLt
  constructor
  · apply Fin.ext
    have hpos : (cfg.inputPos.val : ℤ) +
        (virtualMove (decide (bufferTape [true] (cfg.inputPos.val : ℤ) ≠ some true))
          cfg.inputSymbol d : ℤ) = ((moveInputPos cfg.inputPos d).val : ℤ) := by omega
    have he : (((universalInputPos α x cfg.inputPos).val : ℤ) +
        (virtualMove (decide (bufferTape [true] (cfg.inputPos.val : ℤ) ≠ some true))
          cfg.inputSymbol d : ℤ)).toNat =
        2 * α.length + 2 + (moveInputPos cfg.inputPos d).val := by
      simp only [universalInputPos, Fin.val_mk]
      omega
    unfold moveInputPos
    simp only [he]
    rw [dif_pos (by omega)]
    rfl
  · omega


/-- Capture a machine's emissions on an additional table tape, then transfer
control to a four-tape interpreter. The interpreter sees the original physical
input, not a virtual copy of it. Its other three tapes initially remain blank. -/
def universalCaptureTM {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (M : FinTM Bool) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) : FinTM Bool where
  k := M.k + (1 + 3)
  State := Option M.State ⊕ S
  tm :=
    { q₀ := .inl (some M.tm.q₀)
      tr := fun q inp work => match q with
        | .inl (some q) =>
          let a := M.tm.tr q inp (fun i => work (Fin.castAdd 4 i))
          ⟨a.inputTape, tapeBlocks a.workTapes
            (a.output.map some, if a.output = none then 0 else .pos)
            (fun _ => (none, 0)), none, some (.inl a.state)⟩
        | .inl none => controlAction 0 (some (.inr D.q₀))
        | .inr q => rightAction M.k Sum.inr
            (D.tr q inp (fun i => work (Fin.natAdd M.k i))) }

/-- Complete first-phase configuration of the output-capture wrapper. -/
def universalCaptureCfg {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (M : FinTM Bool) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) {x : List Bool}
    (cfg : Cfg M.k Bool M.State x) :
    Cfg (universalCaptureTM M D).k Bool (universalCaptureTM M D).State x where
  state := some (.inl cfg.state)
  inputPos := cfg.inputPos
  workTapes := tapeBlocks cfg.workTapes (bufferTape cfg.output) (fun _ _ => none)
  workTapePos := tapeBlocks cfg.workTapePos cfg.output.length (fun _ => 0)
  output := []

/-- The capture wrapper starts with a blank table and blank interpreter tapes. -/
private lemma universalCapture_init {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (M : FinTM Bool) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) (x : List Bool) :
    (universalCaptureTM M D).tm.initCfg x =
      universalCaptureCfg M D (M.tm.initCfg x) := by
  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl
  · funext i
    refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ i
    · intro j; simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks]
    · intro j
      refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ j <;> intro j <;>
        simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks]
  · funext i
    refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ i
    · intro j; simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks]
    · intro j
      refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ j <;> intro j <;>
        simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks]

/-- One live transition captures every emitted bit, including a bit emitted on
the source machine's halting transition. Administrative states remain live.

**Proof sketch.** The original work block and physical input move in lockstep.
An emission writes precisely the table's right blank and advances its head; the
buffer-append identity gives its new contents. No real output is emitted, and
the three later simulation tapes remain untouched. -/
private lemma universalCapture_step {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (M : FinTM Bool) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) {x : List Bool}
    (cfg : Cfg M.k Bool M.State x) (hs : cfg.state ≠ none) :
    (universalCaptureTM M D).tm.step (universalCaptureCfg M D cfg) =
      universalCaptureCfg M D (M.tm.step cfg) := by
  unfold MultiTapeTM.step
  cases hq : cfg.state with
  | none => exact False.elim (hs hq)
  | some q =>
    have hs' : (universalCaptureCfg M D cfg).state = some (.inl (some q)) := by
      simp [universalCaptureCfg, hq]
    rw [hs']
    dsimp only [universalCaptureTM]
    have hr : (fun i => (universalCaptureCfg M D cfg).workTapeSymbols
        (Fin.castAdd 4 i)) = cfg.workTapeSymbols := by
      funext i
      simp [universalCaptureCfg, Cfg.workTapeSymbols, tapeBlocks]
    have hi : (universalCaptureCfg M D cfg).inputSymbol = cfg.inputSymbol := rfl
    rw [hr, hi]
    let a := M.tm.tr q cfg.inputSymbol cfg.workTapeSymbols
    change (⟨a.inputTape, tapeBlocks a.workTapes
      (a.output.map some, if a.output = none then 0 else .pos)
      (fun _ => (none, 0)), none, some (.inl a.state)⟩ :
      Action (M.k + (1 + 3)) Bool _).apply _ = universalCaptureCfg M D (a.apply cfg)
    refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ ?_
    · funext i
      refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ i
      · intro j; simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks, Action.apply]
      · intro j
        refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ j
        · intro j
          cases ho : a.output <;>
            simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks, Action.apply, ho, bufferTape_append]
        · intro j; simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks, Action.apply]
    · funext i
      refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ i
      · intro j; simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks, Action.apply]
      · intro j
        refine Fin.addCases ?_ ?_ j
        · intro j
          cases ho : a.output <;> simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks, Action.apply, ho]
        · intro j; simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks, Action.apply]
    · simp [universalCaptureCfg, tapeBlocks, Action.apply]

/-- Lockstep capture through the first halting transition. -/
private lemma universalCapture_run {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (M : FinTM Bool) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) {x : List Bool}
    (cfg : Cfg M.k Bool M.State x) (t : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ s, s < t → (M.tm.runFrom cfg s).state ≠ none) :
    (universalCaptureTM M D).tm.runFrom (universalCaptureCfg M D cfg) t =
      universalCaptureCfg M D (M.tm.runFrom cfg t) := by
  induction t with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (fun s hs => h s (by omega)),
      universalCapture_step M D _ (h t (by omega)), MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']

/-- Capture and interpreter entry preserve the entire halted source configuration
as inactive data, except that its output is now on the table tape. -/
def universalCapturedCfg {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (M : FinTM Bool) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) {x : List Bool}
    (cfg : Cfg M.k Bool M.State x) :
    Cfg (universalCaptureTM M D).k Bool (universalCaptureTM M D).State x :=
  { universalCaptureCfg M D cfg with state := some (.inr D.q₀) }

/-- A halted source configuration transfers to the live interpreter entry state. -/
private lemma universalCapture_transfer {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (M : FinTM Bool) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) {x : List Bool}
    (cfg : Cfg M.k Bool M.State x) (h : cfg.state = none) :
    (universalCaptureTM M D).tm.step (universalCaptureCfg M D cfg) =
      universalCapturedCfg M D cfg := by
  unfold MultiTapeTM.step
  simp only [universalCaptureCfg, h]
  refine Cfg.ext rfl (moveInputPos_zero _) ?_ ?_ ?_
  · rfl
  · funext i; exact add_zero _
  · rfl

/-- Every completed source computation reaches the interpreter with the table
captured in at most one extra transition.

**Proof sketch.** Choose the first source halting time. Lockstep capture holds
through that transition; one live administrative transition enters the interpreter.
Absorbing source halting identifies this first halted configuration with the one
at the supplied time bound, so all its fields (including parked input position)
are retained, not merely its completed output. -/
lemma universalCapture_start {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (M : FinTM Bool) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) (x : List Bool) (T : ℕ)
    (h : (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) T).state = none) :
    ∃ t, t ≤ T + 1 ∧
      (universalCaptureTM M D).tm.runFrom ((universalCaptureTM M D).tm.initCfg x) t =
        universalCapturedCfg M D (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) T) := by
  classical
  have hh : ∃ t, (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).state = none := ⟨T, h⟩
  let t := Nat.find hh
  have ht : t ≤ T := Nat.find_min' hh h
  have hs : (M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t).state = none := Nat.find_spec hh
  have he : M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) T = M.tm.runFrom (M.tm.initCfg x) t := by
    obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le ht
    rw [hd, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt _ hs]
  refine ⟨t + 1, by omega, ?_⟩
  rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', universalCapture_init,
    universalCapture_run M D _ t (fun s hs => Nat.find_min hh hs),
    universalCapture_transfer M D _ hs, he]

/-- Prefix-only startup with the actual canonical table on a work tape. The
input suffix stays in place, unread during startup, and the interpreter receives
three blank work tapes for state, simulated work, and the virtual-left marker.

**Proof sketch.** Compose the configuration-level prefix/canonizer run with the
capture theorem. The bound `3|α|+5+canonizerTime |α|` is independent of the suffix.
The equality is of full configurations, and the three projections explicitly
identify the completed table, the parked physical head, and the still-empty output. -/
private lemma universal_captured_table {S : Type} [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (c : EffectiveMachineCode) (D : MultiTapeTM 4 Bool S) (α x : List Bool) :
    ∃ t, t ≤ 3 * α.length + 5 + c.canonizerTime α.length ∧
      let cfg := (universalCaptureTM (universalCanonTM c) D).tm.runFrom
        ((universalCaptureTM (universalCanonTM c) D).tm.initCfg (pairEncode α x)) t
      cfg.state = some (.inr D.q₀) ∧
      cfg.inputPos.val = 2 * α.length + 3 ∧
      cfg.workTapes (Fin.natAdd (universalCanonTM c).k (0 : Fin 4)) =
        bufferTape (c.decode α).serialize ∧ cfg.output = [] := by
  have hc := universalCanon_complete c α x
  obtain ⟨t, ht, he⟩ := universalCapture_start (universalCanonTM c) D (pairEncode α x)
    (3 * α.length + 4 + c.canonizerTime α.length) hc.1
  refine ⟨t, by omega, ?_⟩
  dsimp only
  rw [he]
  refine ⟨rfl, hc.2.2, ?_, rfl⟩
  change tapeBlocks _ _ _
    (Fin.natAdd (universalCanonTM c).k (Fin.castAdd 3 (0 : Fin 1))) = _
  rw [tapeBlocks_buffer, hc.2.1]

end Turing
```

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machine-construction library: constant writers and native-input sweeps (§12.8)

The single-sweep rows of the §12.8 rich-alphabet design
(`machine-library-design.md` §12.8a) that touch no G1-owned file: two writers
of a fixed word (R8.4, R8.4′) and two sweeps of the native input (R8.5a,
R8.5d). They are alphabet-generic, like the G1 catalog, and they are stated in
the §12.6 framed form: exact time, finish configuration, no earlier exit, and
the trajectory of every head, from an arbitrary configuration.

**Status: proved.** The four framed contracts are proved. The constant writer
and both native-input sweeps instantiate the public catalog trace; the cyclic
advancing writer uses one forward induction.

## Design

* **Two writers.** `Turing.writeConstTM` writes its word and returns the head,
  so it composes under `Turing.seamCompTM` like the R3 sweeps. The advancing
  writer `Turing.writeAdvTM` leaves the head after the word and returns to its
  own start state, which is the round shape of `Turing.counterLoopTM`; it is
  the round of `Turing.expandTM` (R8.6). A seam consumer that calls it once
  uses `Turing.seamReleaseTM`.
* **Tables** are written with the catalog's one-tape actions
  `Turing.tapeAction` and `Turing.inputMoveAction`.
* **The input sweeps** move the native input head and return it to position
  `1`. `Turing.inputCopyTM` moves the destination work head in lockstep with
  it; `Turing.inputFoldTM` moves only the input head, so its work heads stay
  fixed. `Turing.inputCopyTM` reuses the sweep
  alphabet `Turing.SweepPhase` and `Turing.inputFoldTM` the scan alphabet
  `Turing.ScanPhase`, so no phase type is duplicated.
* **The input fold is the validator** of design §12.8a §0: a rich
  space-bounded simulator folds its input through `decodeBool`'s domain first
  and stops on a foreign symbol, because `alphabet_reduction_spaceUsed` bounds
  space over all rich inputs (decision O6).

## Main definitions

* `Turing.WritePhase`, `Turing.writeConstTM` — write a fixed word and return.
* `Turing.writeAdvTM` — write a fixed word and leave the head after it.
* `Turing.inputCopyTM` — copy the native input onto a work tape.
* `Turing.inputFoldTM` — fold the native input with a finite-state update.

## Main results

* `Turing.writeConstTM_run_ofCfg`, `Turing.writeAdvTM_run_ofCfg`,
  `Turing.inputCopyTM_run_ofCfg`, `Turing.inputFoldTM_run_ofCfg` — the framed
  contracts (proved).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2: the k-tape model with a read-only
  input tape; the routines are folklore subroutines of the textbook's
  simulations. §4.1: the space measure that makes input validation necessary
  for the rich simulators.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-- A partially written word, with its arbitrary exterior frame preserved. The three
writing rows share this family; `r` counts written cells, `q` is the control state,
and `p` is the native-input position. -/
private def scanWriteCfg {Symbol S : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol S x) (q : S)
    (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (r : ℕ) : Cfg k Symbol S x :=
  { d with state := some q
           inputPos := p
           workTapes := fun j z =>
             if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ z ∧ z < d.workTapePos j + (r : ℤ)
               then FinTM.bufferTape w (z - d.workTapePos j) else d.workTapes j z
           workTapePos := fun j => d.workTapePos j + if j = i then (r : ℤ) else 0 }

/-- Writing the next symbol and moving right extends the shared written prefix.

**Proof sketch.** Cite the public writing-step equation. On the selected tape,
`catalog_write_take` extends the overwrite interval by one cell; all other tapes
are fixed, and the selected head advances by one. -/
private theorem scan_write_step {Symbol S : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (M : MultiTapeTM k Symbol S) (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol S x)
    (q q' : S) (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (inp : SignType) (r : ℕ) (hr : r < w.length)
    (htr : M.tr q (scanWriteCfg i w d q p r).inputSymbol
        (scanWriteCfg i w d q p r).workTapeSymbols =
      tapeAction i inp (some (some w[r])) .pos q') :
    M.step (scanWriteCfg i w d q p r) =
      scanWriteCfg i w d q' (moveInputPos p inp) (r + 1) := by
  rw [step_of_tapeAction_write M _ i inp _ .pos rfl htr]
  apply Cfg.ext
  case workTapes =>
    funext j
    by_cases hj : j = i
    · subst j
      simpa [scanWriteCfg] using catalog_write_take (d.workTapes i) (d.workTapePos i) w r hr
    · simp [scanWriteCfg, hj]
  case workTapePos =>
    funext j
    by_cases hj : j = i <;>
      simp [scanWriteCfg, hj, Function.update_apply, SignType.cast] <;> omega
  all_goals simp [scanWriteCfg]

/-! ### R8.4 — the constant writer -/

/-- **Phase alphabet of the constant writer** (design §12.8a, R8.4), for a word
of length `n`: writing cell `j`, walking back with `j` cells to go, and the
live exit anchor. -/
inductive WritePhase (n : ℕ) where
  /-- writing cell `j` of the word -/
  | wr (j : Fin (n + 1))
  /-- walking back, `j` cells from the origin -/
  | bk (j : Fin (n + 1))
  /-- the live exit anchor -/
  | done
deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- **R8.4, the constant writer** (design §12.8a). Write the fixed word `w₀` on
tape `i` from its head, moving right, then walk back `|w₀|` cells and enter the
live `done` anchor with the head where it started. The old contents of the
tape are never read. -/
def writeConstTM {Symbol : Type*} (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (w₀ : List Symbol) :
    MultiTapeTM k Symbol (WritePhase w₀.length) where
  q₀ := .wr 0
  tr := fun q _ _ =>
    match q with
    | .wr j =>
      if h : (j : ℕ) < w₀.length then
        tapeAction i 0 (some (some w₀[(j : ℕ)])) .pos (.wr ⟨j + 1, by omega⟩)
      else inputMoveAction 0 (.bk ⟨w₀.length, by omega⟩)
    | .bk j =>
      if (j : ℕ) = 0 then inputMoveAction 0 .done
      else tapeAction i 0 none .neg (.bk ⟨j - 1, by omega⟩)
    | .done => inputMoveAction 0 .done

/-- The constant writer after `r` forward steps, with a total finite-state index. -/
private def scanConstF {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w.length) x) (r : ℕ) :
    Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w.length) x :=
  scanWriteCfg i w d (.wr ⟨min r w.length, by omega⟩) d.inputPos r

/-- The constant writer's return configuration, `r` cells to the right of entry. -/
private def scanConstR {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w.length) x) (r : ℕ) :
    Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w.length) x :=
  { scanWriteCfg i w d (.bk ⟨min r w.length, by omega⟩) d.inputPos w.length with
      workTapePos := fun j => d.workTapePos j + if j = i then (r : ℤ) else 0 }

/-- The constant writer's exit, with the entire word written and all heads restored. -/
private def scanConstD {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w.length) x) :
    Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w.length) x :=
  { d with state := some .done
           workTapes := (scanConstF i w d w.length).workTapes }

/-- The constant writer instantiates the public two-pass trace.

**Proof sketch.** The shared write step supplies the forward equations. A stationary
turn enters the return family; left moves count down to zero; a stationary entry
reaches the fixed exit. The public trace theorem supplies the whole run. -/
private theorem scan_const_trace {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w.length) x)
    (hstate : d.state = some (.wr 0)) (t : ℕ) :
    (writeConstTM k i w).runFrom d t =
      catalogTrace (scanConstF i w d) (scanConstR i w d) (scanConstD i w d) w.length t := by
  have h0 : scanConstF i w d 0 = d := by
    apply Cfg.ext
    case workTapes => funext j z; simp [scanConstF, scanWriteCfg]
    all_goals simp [scanConstF, scanWriteCfg, hstate]
  conv_lhs => rw [← h0]
  apply catalog_trace_run
  · intro r hr
    unfold scanConstF
    simpa only [moveInputPos_zero] using
      scan_write_step (writeConstTM k i w) i w d (.wr ⟨min r w.length, by omega⟩)
        (.wr ⟨min (r + 1) w.length, by omega⟩) d.inputPos 0 r hr (by
          simp only [writeConstTM]
          rw [dif_pos (show min r w.length < w.length by omega)]
          simp only [show min r w.length = r by omega]
          congr 2
          apply Fin.ext
          simp
          omega)
  · rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ 0 rfl
      (q' := .bk ⟨min w.length w.length, by omega⟩) (by
        simp only [writeConstTM]
        rw [dif_neg (show ¬ min w.length w.length < w.length by omega)]
        simp)]
    apply Cfg.ext <;> simp [scanConstF, scanConstR, scanWriteCfg]
  · intro r hr
    rw [step_of_tapeAction_move _ _ i 0 .neg rfl
      (q' := .bk ⟨min r w.length, by omega⟩) (by
        simp only [writeConstTM]
        rw [if_neg (show ¬ min (r + 1) w.length = 0 by omega)]
        congr 2
        apply Fin.ext
        simp
        omega)]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case workTapePos =>
      funext j
      by_cases hj : j = i <;>
        simp [scanConstR, scanWriteCfg, hj, Function.update_apply] <;> omega
    all_goals simp [scanConstR, scanWriteCfg]
  · rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ 0 rfl (q' := .done) (by simp [writeConstTM])]
    apply Cfg.ext <;> simp [scanConstR, scanConstD, scanConstF, scanWriteCfg]
  · rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ 0 rfl (q' := .done) rfl]
    simp [scanConstD]

/-- **R8.4, the constant writer, framed** (design §12.8a). From any
configuration at the writer's start phase, the writer reaches `done` at
exactly `2|w₀| + 2` and not earlier. At that point the interval
`[pos, pos + |w₀|)` of tape `i` holds `w₀`, whatever it held before, and every
other cell, the head positions, the input position and the output are
unchanged. Up to the exit the head of tape `i` stays within
`[pos, pos + |w₀|]`, and every other head is fixed.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the cells written: `|w₀|` steps write `w₀` moving
right. One stationary step turns into the walk back, `|w₀|` steps return the
head to `pos`, and one stationary step enters `done`. No step reads a work
cell, so the old contents are irrelevant. -/
theorem writeConstTM_run_ofCfg {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (i : Fin k)
    (w₀ : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (WritePhase w₀.length) x)
    (hstate : d.state = some (.wr 0)) :
    (writeConstTM k i w₀).runFrom d (2 * w₀.length + 2) =
        { d with
          state := some .done
          workTapes := fun j q =>
            if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + (w₀.length : ℤ)
              then FinTM.bufferTape w₀ (q - d.workTapePos j)
            else d.workTapes j q } ∧
      (∀ t < 2 * w₀.length + 2, ((writeConstTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).state ≠ some .done) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ 2 * w₀.length + 2 →
        if j = i then
          ((writeConstTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j) (d.workTapePos j + (w₀.length : ℤ))
        else ((writeConstTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [scan_const_trace i w₀ d hstate]
    simp [catalogTrace, scanConstD, scanConstF, scanWriteCfg,
      show ¬2 * w₀.length + 2 ≤ w₀.length by omega]
  · intro t ht
    rw [scan_const_trace i w₀ d hstate]
    simp only [catalogTrace]
    split_ifs <;> simp [scanConstF, scanConstR, scanConstD, scanWriteCfg] <;> omega
  · intro j t ht
    rw [scan_const_trace i w₀ d hstate]
    simp only [catalogTrace]
    split_ifs <;>
      simp_all [scanConstF, scanConstR, scanConstD, scanWriteCfg, Finset.mem_Icc] <;> omega

/-! ### R8.4′ — the advancing writer -/

/-- **R8.4′, the advancing writer** (design §12.8a). Write the fixed word `w₀`
on tape `i` from its head, moving right, and return to the start state `0` with
the head just after the word. The state `j` is the number of cells written. The
writer is cyclic: started again, it writes `w₀` again after the first copy,
which makes it a round body of `Turing.counterLoopTM` with anchor `0`. -/
def writeAdvTM {Symbol : Type*} (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) (w₀ : List Symbol) :
    MultiTapeTM k Symbol (Fin (w₀.length + 1)) where
  q₀ := 0
  tr := fun j _ _ =>
    if h : (j : ℕ) < w₀.length then
      tapeAction i 0 (some (some w₀[(j : ℕ)])) .pos ⟨j + 1, by omega⟩
    else inputMoveAction 0 0

/-- The advancing writer after `r` writes; its finite state counts the written cells. -/
private def scanAdvF {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (Fin (w.length + 1)) x) (r : ℕ) :
    Cfg k Symbol (Fin (w.length + 1)) x :=
  scanWriteCfg i w d ⟨min r w.length, by omega⟩ d.inputPos r

/-- Up to the word length, the advancing writer follows the shared write family.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the number of written cells, invoking `scan_write_step`
at each successor. This is a single forward induction: the cyclic exit is not
stationary, so the two-pass trace theorem does not apply. -/
private theorem scan_adv_run {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (w : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (Fin (w.length + 1)) x)
    (hstate : d.state = some 0) :
    ∀ r ≤ w.length, (writeAdvTM k i w).runFrom d r = scanAdvF i w d r := by
  intro r hr
  induction r with
  | zero =>
    apply Cfg.ext
    case workTapes => funext j z; simp [scanAdvF, scanWriteCfg]
    all_goals simp [scanAdvF, scanWriteCfg, hstate]
  | succ r ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (by omega)]
    unfold scanAdvF
    simpa only [moveInputPos_zero] using
      scan_write_step (writeAdvTM k i w) i w d ⟨min r w.length, by omega⟩
        ⟨min (r + 1) w.length, by omega⟩ d.inputPos 0 r (by omega) (by
          simp only [writeAdvTM]
          rw [dif_pos (show min r w.length < w.length by omega)]
          simp only [show min r w.length = r by omega]
          congr 1
          apply Fin.ext
          simp
          omega)

/-- **R8.4′, the advancing writer, framed** (design §12.8a). From any
configuration at state `0`, the writer returns to state `0` at exactly
`|w₀| + 1`, and its states strictly between are not `0`. At that point the
interval `[pos, pos + |w₀|)` of tape `i` holds `w₀`, whatever it held before,
the head of tape `i` is at `pos + |w₀|`, and every other cell, every other
head, the input position and the output are unchanged. Up to the return the
head of tape `i` stays within `[pos, pos + |w₀|]`, and every other head is
fixed. These are exactly the round hypotheses of `Turing.counterLoopTM_run_done`
with round time `|w₀| + 1`.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the cells written: the state after `j ≤ |w₀|` steps
is `j`, which is nonzero for `0 < j`, with `j` cells of `w₀` written and the
head at `pos + j`. The last step is stationary and returns to `0`. No step
reads a work cell. -/
theorem writeAdvTM_run_ofCfg {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (i : Fin k)
    (w₀ : List Symbol) (d : Cfg k Symbol (Fin (w₀.length + 1)) x)
    (hstate : d.state = some 0) :
    (writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d (w₀.length + 1) =
        { d with
          state := some 0
          workTapes := fun j q =>
            if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + (w₀.length : ℤ)
              then FinTM.bufferTape w₀ (q - d.workTapePos j)
            else d.workTapes j q
          workTapePos := Function.update d.workTapePos i
            (d.workTapePos i + (w₀.length : ℤ)) } ∧
      (∀ t, 0 < t → t < w₀.length + 1 → ((writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).state ≠ some 0) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ w₀.length + 1 →
        if j = i then
          ((writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j) (d.workTapePos j + (w₀.length : ℤ))
        else ((writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
  have hlast : (writeAdvTM k i w₀).runFrom d (w₀.length + 1) =
      { scanAdvF i w₀ d w₀.length with state := some 0 } := by
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', scan_adv_run i w₀ d hstate _ le_rfl]
    rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ 0 rfl (q' := 0) (by
      simp only [writeAdvTM]
      rw [dif_neg (show ¬ min w₀.length w₀.length < w₀.length by omega)])]
    simp
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [hlast]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case workTapePos =>
      funext j
      by_cases hj : j = i
      · subst j; simp [scanAdvF, scanWriteCfg]
      · simp [scanAdvF, scanWriteCfg, hj]
    all_goals simp [scanAdvF, scanWriteCfg]
  · intro t ht0 ht
    rw [scan_adv_run i w₀ d hstate t (by omega)]
    simp only [scanAdvF, scanWriteCfg, ne_eq, Option.some.injEq, Fin.ext_iff, Fin.val_zero]
    omega
  · intro j t ht
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge t (w₀.length + 1) with h | h
    · rw [scan_adv_run i w₀ d hstate t (by omega)]
      split_ifs with hj <;> simp [scanAdvF, scanWriteCfg, hj, Finset.mem_Icc] <;> omega
    · rw [show t = w₀.length + 1 by omega, hlast]
      split_ifs with hj <;> simp [scanAdvF, scanWriteCfg, hj, Finset.mem_Icc]

/-! ### R8.5a — the input copier -/

/-- **R8.5a, the input copier** (design §12.8a). Copy the native input onto
tape `i` from its head, the two heads moving right in lockstep, then walk both
heads back together, guided by the input tape's left end marker. The phases are
the sweep alphabet's: `sweep` copies, `rewind` returns, and `done` is the live
exit anchor. The destination needs no left delimiter. -/
def inputCopyTM {Symbol : Type*} (k : ℕ) (i : Fin k) : MultiTapeTM k Symbol SweepPhase where
  q₀ := .sweep
  tr := fun q inp _ =>
    match q with
    | .sweep =>
      match inp with
      | some s => tapeAction i 1 (some (some s)) .pos .sweep
      | none => tapeAction i (-1) none .neg .rewind
    | .rewind =>
      match inp with
      | some _ => tapeAction i (-1) none .neg .rewind
      | none => tapeAction i 1 none .pos .done
    | .done => inputMoveAction 0 .done

/-- The copier after `r` forward steps, with the input and destination heads advanced. -/
private def scanCopyF {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (r : ℕ) : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x :=
  scanWriteCfg i x d .sweep ⟨min r x.length + 1, by omega⟩ r

/-- The copier's return family, indexed by native-input position down to zero. -/
private def scanCopyR {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (r : ℕ) : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x :=
  { scanWriteCfg i x d .rewind ⟨min r x.length, by omega⟩ x.length with
      workTapePos := fun j => d.workTapePos j + if j = i then (r : ℤ) - 1 else 0 }

/-- The copier's exit restores both heads while retaining the copied input. -/
private def scanCopyD {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x :=
  { d with state := some .done
           workTapes := (scanCopyF i d x.length).workTapes }

/-- The native-input copier instantiates the public two-pass trace.

**Proof sketch.** Interior input reads supply the symbols for the shared write
step. The right marker turns both heads left, interior reads guide the return,
and the left marker moves both heads right into the fixed exit. No destination
delimiter is used. Apply the public trace theorem to these five equations. -/
private theorem scan_copy_trace {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol}
    (i : Fin k) (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x)
    (hstate : d.state = some .sweep) (hin : d.inputPos = 1) (t : ℕ) :
    (inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d t =
      catalogTrace (scanCopyF i d) (scanCopyR i d) (scanCopyD i d) x.length t := by
  have h0 : scanCopyF i d 0 = d := by
    apply Cfg.ext
    case inputPos => rw [hin]; apply Fin.ext; simp [scanCopyF, scanWriteCfg]
    case workTapes => funext j z; simp [scanCopyF, scanWriteCfg]
    all_goals simp [scanCopyF, scanWriteCfg, hstate]
  conv_lhs => rw [← h0]
  apply catalog_trace_run
  · intro r hr
    have hs : (scanCopyF i d r).inputSymbol = some x[r] :=
      inputSymbolInner r (by simp [scanCopyF, scanWriteCfg]; omega) hr
    unfold scanCopyF
    rw [scan_write_step (inputCopyTM k i) i x d .sweep .sweep _ 1 r hr
      (by
        change (inputCopyTM k i).tr .sweep (scanCopyF i d r).inputSymbol
          (scanCopyF i d r).workTapeSymbols = _
        simp only [inputCopyTM, hs])]
    congr 1
    rw [← SignType.pos_eq_one, moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp; omega)]
    simp
    omega
  · have hs : (scanCopyF i d x.length).inputSymbol = none := by
      simp [Cfg.inputSymbol, scanCopyF, scanWriteCfg]
    rw [step_of_tapeAction_move _ _ i (-1) .neg rfl (q' := .rewind)
      (by simp only [inputCopyTM, hs])]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case inputPos =>
      simp only [scanCopyF, scanCopyR, scanWriteCfg]
      apply Fin.ext
      rw [← SignType.neg_eq_neg_one, FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val]
      simp
    case workTapePos =>
      funext j
      by_cases hj : j = i <;>
        simp [scanCopyF, scanCopyR, scanWriteCfg, hj, Function.update_apply] <;> omega
    all_goals simp [scanCopyF, scanCopyR, scanWriteCfg]
  · intro r hr
    have hs : (scanCopyR i d (r + 1)).inputSymbol = some x[r] :=
      inputSymbolInner r (by simp [scanCopyR, scanWriteCfg]; omega) hr
    rw [step_of_tapeAction_move _ _ i (-1) .neg rfl (q' := .rewind)
      (by simp only [inputCopyTM, hs])]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case inputPos =>
      simp only [scanCopyR, scanWriteCfg]
      apply Fin.ext
      rw [← SignType.neg_eq_neg_one, FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val]
      simp
      omega
    case workTapePos =>
      funext j
      by_cases hj : j = i <;>
        simp [scanCopyR, scanWriteCfg, hj, Function.update_apply] <;> omega
    all_goals simp [scanCopyR, scanWriteCfg]
  · have hs : (scanCopyR i d 0).inputSymbol = none := by
      simp [Cfg.inputSymbol, scanCopyR, scanWriteCfg]
    rw [step_of_tapeAction_move _ _ i 1 .pos rfl (q' := .done)
      (by simp only [inputCopyTM, hs])]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case inputPos =>
      simp only [scanCopyR, scanCopyD, scanWriteCfg, hin]
      rw [← SignType.pos_eq_one, moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp)]
      apply Fin.ext
      simp
    case workTapePos =>
      funext j
      by_cases hj : j = i <;>
        simp [scanCopyR, scanCopyD, scanWriteCfg, hj, Function.update_apply]
    all_goals simp [scanCopyR, scanCopyD, scanCopyF, scanWriteCfg]
  · rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ 0 rfl (q' := .done) rfl]
    simp [scanCopyD]

/-- **R8.5a, the input copier, framed** (design §12.8a). From any configuration
in the copy phase with the input head at position `1`, the copier reaches
`done` at exactly `2|x| + 2` and not earlier, where `x` is the native input. At
that point the interval `[pos, pos + |x|)` of tape `i` holds `x`, whatever it
held before, and every other cell, every head, the input position and the
output are unchanged. Up to the exit the head of tape `i` stays within
`[pos - 1, pos + |x|]`, and every other head is fixed.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the input cells: `|x|` lockstep steps copy `x`,
and the input's right end marker turns both heads left. The return takes `|x|`
lockstep steps over the input, and the left end marker supplies the entry step,
which puts the input head back at `1` and the work head back at `pos`. -/
theorem inputCopyTM_run_ofCfg {Symbol : Type*} {k : ℕ} {x : List Symbol} (i : Fin k)
    (d : Cfg k Symbol SweepPhase x) (hstate : d.state = some .sweep) (hin : d.inputPos = 1) :
    (inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d (2 * x.length + 2) =
        { d with
          state := some .done
          workTapes := fun j q =>
            if j = i ∧ d.workTapePos j ≤ q ∧ q < d.workTapePos j + (x.length : ℤ)
              then FinTM.bufferTape x (q - d.workTapePos j)
            else d.workTapes j q } ∧
      (∀ t < 2 * x.length + 2, ((inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d t).state ≠ some .done) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ 2 * x.length + 2 →
        if j = i then
          ((inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j ∈
            Finset.Icc (d.workTapePos j - 1) (d.workTapePos j + (x.length : ℤ))
        else ((inputCopyTM k i).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [scan_copy_trace i d hstate hin]
    simp [catalogTrace, scanCopyD, scanCopyF, scanWriteCfg,
      show ¬2 * x.length + 2 ≤ x.length by omega]
  · intro t ht
    rw [scan_copy_trace i d hstate hin]
    simp only [catalogTrace]
    split_ifs <;> simp [scanCopyF, scanCopyR, scanCopyD, scanWriteCfg] <;> omega
  · intro j t ht
    rw [scan_copy_trace i d hstate hin]
    simp only [catalogTrace]
    split_ifs <;>
      simp_all [scanCopyF, scanCopyR, scanCopyD, scanWriteCfg, Finset.mem_Icc] <;> omega

/-! ### R8.5d — the input fold -/

/-- **R8.5d, the input fold** (design §12.8a). Read the native input left to
right, updating a finite state by `δ` from `a₀`, then walk the input head back
and enter the live anchor `done a` with the final state `a` as the verdict.
No work tape is touched. With `δ` testing membership in the image of an
embedding, it is the input validator of design §12.8a §0. -/
def inputFoldTM {Γ : Type*} {A : Type} (k : ℕ) (δ : A → Γ → A) (a₀ : A) :
    MultiTapeTM k Γ (ScanPhase A) where
  q₀ := .fwd a₀
  tr := fun q inp _ =>
    match q with
    | .fwd a =>
      match inp with
      | some γ => inputMoveAction 1 (.fwd (δ a γ))
      | none => inputMoveAction (-1) (.bwd a)
    | .bwd a =>
      match inp with
      | some _ => inputMoveAction (-1) (.bwd a)
      | none => inputMoveAction 1 (.done a)
    | .done a => inputMoveAction 0 (.done a)

/-- The native fold's forward accumulator and input position after `r` reads. -/
private def scanFoldF {Γ : Type*} {A : Type} {k : ℕ} {x : List Γ}
    (δ : A → Γ → A) (a₀ : A) (d : Cfg k Γ (ScanPhase A) x) (r : ℕ) :
    Cfg k Γ (ScanPhase A) x :=
  { d with state := some (.fwd ((x.take r).foldl δ a₀))
           inputPos := ⟨min r x.length + 1, by omega⟩ }

/-- The native fold's return keeps the completed accumulator and counts input positions down. -/
private def scanFoldR {Γ : Type*} {A : Type} {k : ℕ} {x : List Γ}
    (δ : A → Γ → A) (a₀ : A) (d : Cfg k Γ (ScanPhase A) x) (r : ℕ) :
    Cfg k Γ (ScanPhase A) x :=
  { d with state := some (.bwd (x.foldl δ a₀))
           inputPos := ⟨min r x.length, by omega⟩ }

/-- The native fold is an instance of the public two-pass trace, with untouched work tapes.

**Proof sketch.** Interior input reads extend the prefix fold by one symbol. The
right marker changes to the backward phase without changing the final accumulator.
The return passes over the input and enters the fixed verdict at its left marker.
All five equations cite the public input-only step lemma. -/
private theorem scan_fold_trace {Γ : Type*} {A : Type} {k : ℕ} {x : List Γ}
    (δ : A → Γ → A) (a₀ : A) (d : Cfg k Γ (ScanPhase A) x)
    (hstate : d.state = some (.fwd a₀)) (hin : d.inputPos = 1) (t : ℕ) :
    (inputFoldTM k δ a₀).runFrom d t =
      catalogTrace (scanFoldF δ a₀ d) (scanFoldR δ a₀ d)
        { d with state := some (.done (x.foldl δ a₀)) } x.length t := by
  have h0 : scanFoldF δ a₀ d 0 = d := by
    apply Cfg.ext <;> simp [scanFoldF, hstate, hin]
  conv_lhs => rw [← h0]
  apply catalog_trace_run
  · intro r hr
    have hs : (scanFoldF δ a₀ d r).inputSymbol = some x[r] :=
      inputSymbolInner r (by simp [scanFoldF]; omega) hr
    rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ 1 rfl
      (q' := .fwd (δ ((x.take r).foldl δ a₀) x[r])) (by simp only [inputFoldTM, hs])]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case state =>
      simp only [scanFoldF]
      rw [List.take_succ, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hr, List.foldl_append]
      rfl
    case inputPos =>
      simp only [scanFoldF]
      rw [← SignType.pos_eq_one, moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp; omega)]
      simp
      omega
    all_goals simp [scanFoldF]
  · have hs : (scanFoldF δ a₀ d x.length).inputSymbol = none := by
      simp [Cfg.inputSymbol, scanFoldF]
    rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ (-1) rfl
      (q' := .bwd ((x.take x.length).foldl δ a₀)) (by simp only [inputFoldTM, hs])]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case inputPos =>
      simp only [scanFoldF, scanFoldR]
      apply Fin.ext
      rw [← SignType.neg_eq_neg_one, FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val]
      simp
    all_goals simp [scanFoldF, scanFoldR]
  · intro r hr
    have hs : (scanFoldR δ a₀ d (r + 1)).inputSymbol = some x[r] :=
      inputSymbolInner r (by simp [scanFoldR]; omega) hr
    rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ (-1) rfl
      (q' := .bwd (x.foldl δ a₀)) (by simp only [inputFoldTM, hs])]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case inputPos =>
      simp only [scanFoldR]
      apply Fin.ext
      rw [← SignType.neg_eq_neg_one, FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val]
      simp
      omega
    all_goals simp [scanFoldR]
  · have hs : (scanFoldR δ a₀ d 0).inputSymbol = none := by
      simp [Cfg.inputSymbol, scanFoldR]
    rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ 1 rfl
      (q' := .done (x.foldl δ a₀)) (by simp only [inputFoldTM, hs])]
    apply Cfg.ext
    case inputPos =>
      simp only [scanFoldR, hin]
      rw [← SignType.pos_eq_one, moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp)]
      apply Fin.ext
      simp
    all_goals simp [scanFoldR]
  · rw [step_of_inputMoveAction _ _ 0 rfl (q' := .done (x.foldl δ a₀)) rfl]
    simp

/-- **R8.5d, the input fold, framed** (design §12.8a). From any configuration
in the forward phase at `a₀` with the input head at position `1`, the fold
reaches `done (x.foldl δ a₀)` at exactly `2|x| + 2`, where `x` is the native
input, and no `done` anchor earlier. Nothing else changes: the finish is the
start configuration with only the control state replaced, so the input head is
back at `1`. Up to the exit no work head moves.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the input cells: after `j ≤ |x|` forward steps the
state is the fold of the first `j` symbols and the input head is at `j + 1`.
The right end marker turns the head, `|x|` steps return it, and the left end
marker supplies the entry step. -/
theorem inputFoldTM_run_ofCfg {Γ : Type*} {A : Type} {k : ℕ} {x : List Γ}
    (δ : A → Γ → A) (a₀ : A) (d : Cfg k Γ (ScanPhase A) x)
    (hstate : d.state = some (.fwd a₀)) (hin : d.inputPos = 1) :
    (inputFoldTM k δ a₀).runFrom d (2 * x.length + 2) =
        { d with state := some (.done (x.foldl δ a₀)) } ∧
      (∀ t < 2 * x.length + 2, ∀ a,
        ((inputFoldTM k δ a₀).runFrom d t).state ≠ some (.done a)) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin k) (t : ℕ), t ≤ 2 * x.length + 2 →
        ((inputFoldTM k δ a₀).runFrom d t).workTapePos j = d.workTapePos j) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [scan_fold_trace δ a₀ d hstate hin]
    simp [catalogTrace, show ¬2 * x.length + 2 ≤ x.length by omega]
  · intro t ht a
    rw [scan_fold_trace δ a₀ d hstate hin]
    simp only [catalogTrace]
    split_ifs <;> simp [scanFoldF, scanFoldR] <;> omega
  · intro j t _
    rw [scan_fold_trace δ a₀ d hstate hin]
    simp only [catalogTrace]
    split_ifs <;> simp [scanFoldF, scanFoldR]

end Turing
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/SymbolLift.lean (at the gate head) =====

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Finite
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Simulation

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Running `Bool` machines on rich alphabets: the embedding transport

A machine over a rich work alphabet `Γ` often needs a binary routine (a counter, a
compare) on one of its tapes. Instead of re-proving each binary routine at `Γ`, this file
**lifts** a `Bool` machine along an embedding `e : Bool ↪ Γ`. The lifted machine reads
through `decodeBool e`, where foreign symbols read as blank, and writes and emits
through `e`. From every lifted configuration and at every time it runs as the original,
everything mapped along `e` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom`). It is the
embedding analogue of the equivalence transport `Turing.MultiTapeTM.mapWorkSymbols`
(`Build/CounterLoop.lean`). Space is preserved exactly. A lifted computation is a
computation *via* `e` in the sense `Turing.FinTM.alphabet_reduction` consumes, so a
rich-alphabet construction can finish by alphabet reduction.

Design: `machine-library-design.md` §12.8 (decision 12.8.1, rich-alphabet configuration
records) and §12.8a R8.0. Consumers: the §12.8 record rows, which run the binary counter
rows on dedicated digit tapes, and §13d's zone carrier, whose alphabet embeds `Bool` by
`Sum.inl`.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.decodeBool` — decoding along `e`; foreign symbols decode to `none`.
* `Turing.Action.liftSymbols`, `Turing.Cfg.liftSymbols`, `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols`,
  `Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols` — the lift of actions, configurations and machines.

## Main results

* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom` — the transport: lifted runs are lifts of runs.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step` — its one-step form.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_initCfg`, `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_spaceUsed` — start
  configurations and space.
* `Turing.FinTM.liftSymbols_computesFunInTimeVia` — a lifted computation is a computation via
  `e`, in the same time.
* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom_over`, with `Turing.Cfg.liftOver`,
  `Turing.Cfg.decodeSymbols` and `Turing.Cfg.liftOver_decodeSymbols` — the overlay transport:
  a lifted run of an input-oblivious, blank-free table from an arbitrary rich configuration,
  keeping its rich frame (§12.8 fill, for R8.0b and the record rows).
* `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_map`, `Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_map_decode`,
  `Turing.decodeBool_eq_some` — delimited words and decoding under the lift.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*, Cambridge
  University Press, 2009. (§1.2 and Claim 1.5: the alphabet of a machine can be changed at a
  constant-factor cost; this file is the cost-free direction, from `Bool` into a larger
  alphabet.)
-/

namespace Turing

section Lift
variable {k : ℕ} {Γ State : Type*}

/-- Decode a rich symbol along `e : Bool ↪ Γ`: `e b` decodes to `some b`, and every
symbol outside the image of `e` decodes to `none`, which the lifted machine reads as a
blank. -/
def decodeBool [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (γ : Γ) : Option Bool :=
  if γ = e true then some true else if γ = e false then some false else none

/-- Decoding inverts `e` on its image.

**Proof sketch.** `cases b`; the two images differ by injectivity of `e`. -/
@[simp] lemma decodeBool_apply [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (b : Bool) :
    decodeBool e (e b) = some b := by
  cases b
  · have : e false ≠ e true := fun h => Bool.false_ne_true (e.injective h)
    simp [decodeBool, this]
  · simp [decodeBool]

/-- Lift an action along `e`: written symbols and the emission are mapped by `e`. -/
def Action.liftSymbols (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (a : Action k Bool State) : Action k Γ State where
  inputTape := a.inputTape
  workTapes := fun j => ((a.workTapes j).1.map (Option.map e), (a.workTapes j).2)
  output := a.output.map e
  state := a.state

/-- Lift a configuration along `e`: input, work cells and output mapped by `e`. -/
def Cfg.liftSymbols (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) :
    Cfg k Γ State (x.map e) where
  state := c.state
  inputPos := Fin.cast (by simp) c.inputPos
  workTapes := fun j p => (c.workTapes j p).map e
  workTapePos := c.workTapePos
  output := c.output.map e

/-- Lift a machine along `e`: read through `decodeBool e`, write through `e`. -/
def MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State) (e : Bool ↪ Γ) :
    MultiTapeTM k Γ State where
  q₀ := M.q₀
  tr := fun q inp work =>
    (M.tr q (inp.bind (decodeBool e)) fun j => (work j).bind (decodeBool e)).liftSymbols e

/-- The lifted configuration reads the mapped input symbol.

**Proof sketch.** The two input positions have the same value, so the end-marker cases
match; an inner position reads `(x.map e)[i] = e x[i]`. -/
lemma Cfg.liftSymbols_inputSymbol (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) :
    (c.liftSymbols e).inputSymbol = c.inputSymbol.map e := by
  have hv : ((c.liftSymbols e).inputPos : ℕ) = c.inputPos := rfl
  unfold Cfg.inputSymbol
  have e0 : ((c.liftSymbols e).inputPos = 0) ↔ (c.inputPos = 0) := by
    simp only [Fin.ext_iff, hv, Fin.val_zero]
  have e1 : ((c.liftSymbols e).inputPos = ((x.map e).length + 1 : ℕ)) ↔
      (c.inputPos = (x.length + 1 : ℕ)) := by
    simp only [hv, List.length_map]
  by_cases h0 : c.inputPos = 0
  · rw [dif_pos (e0.mpr h0), dif_pos h0]; rfl
  · rw [dif_neg (fun h => h0 (e0.mp h)), dif_neg h0]
    by_cases h1 : c.inputPos = (x.length + 1 : ℕ)
    · rw [dif_pos (e1.mpr h1), dif_pos h1]; rfl
    · rw [dif_neg (fun h => h1 (e1.mp h)), dif_neg h1]
      simp [hv]

/-- Moving the input head commutes with recasting the position type. -/
private lemma moveInputPos_cast {n m : ℕ} (h : n + 2 = m + 2) (p : Fin (n + 2)) (s : SignType) :
    moveInputPos (Fin.cast h p) s = Fin.cast h (moveInputPos p s) := by
  have hnm : n = m := by omega
  subst hnm
  rfl

/-- One step commutes with the lift.

**Proof sketch.** A halted configuration does not move. Otherwise the lifted machine
decodes the scanned symbols back to the original ones (`decodeBool_apply`), so it
selects the lift of the original action; applying a lifted action to a lifted
configuration is the lift of the applied action, cell by cell. -/
lemma MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State)
    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) :
    (M.liftSymbols e).step (c.liftSymbols e) = (M.step c).liftSymbols e := by
  cases hs : c.state with
  | none => simp [MultiTapeTM.step, Cfg.liftSymbols, hs]
  | some q =>
    have hin : (c.liftSymbols e).inputSymbol.bind (decodeBool e) = c.inputSymbol := by
      rw [Cfg.liftSymbols_inputSymbol]; cases c.inputSymbol <;> simp
    have hw : (fun j => ((c.liftSymbols e).workTapeSymbols j).bind (decodeBool e)) =
        c.workTapeSymbols := by
      funext j; simp only [Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Cfg.liftSymbols]
      cases c.workTapes j (c.workTapePos j) <;> simp
    simp only [MultiTapeTM.step,
      show (c.liftSymbols e).state = some q by simp [Cfg.liftSymbols, hs], hs]
    change ((M.tr q ((c.liftSymbols e).inputSymbol.bind (decodeBool e))
      fun j => ((c.liftSymbols e).workTapeSymbols j).bind (decodeBool e)).liftSymbols e).apply
        (c.liftSymbols e) = _
    rw [hin, hw]
    apply Cfg.ext
    · rfl
    · exact moveInputPos_cast (by simp) _ _
    · funext j p
      simp only [Action.apply, Action.liftSymbols, Cfg.liftSymbols]
      cases (M.tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols).workTapes j |>.1 with
      | none => simp
      | some v =>
        simp only [Option.map_some]
        by_cases hp : p = c.workTapePos j
        · subst p; simp
        · simp [Function.update_of_ne hp]
    · rfl
    · simp only [Action.apply, Action.liftSymbols, Cfg.liftSymbols, List.map_append]
      cases (M.tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols).output <;> rfl

/-- **The embedding transport** (§12.8 R8.0): from every `Bool` configuration and at
every time, the lifted machine runs as the original, with input, work cells and output
mapped along `e`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `t` with `liftSymbols_step`. -/
theorem MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State)
    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) (t : ℕ) :
    (M.liftSymbols e).runFrom (c.liftSymbols e) t = (M.runFrom c t).liftSymbols e := by
  induction t generalizing c with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step,
      MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step, ih]

/-- The lift keeps the state. -/
@[simp] lemma Cfg.liftSymbols_state (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) :
    (c.liftSymbols e).state = c.state := rfl

/-- The lift keeps the work-head positions. -/
@[simp] lemma Cfg.liftSymbols_workTapePos (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool}
    (c : Cfg k Bool State x) : (c.liftSymbols e).workTapePos = c.workTapePos := rfl

/-- The lifted machine starts at the lift of the original start (both blank tapes, same
heads and state). -/
lemma MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_initCfg [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State)
    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (x : List Bool) :
    (M.liftSymbols e).initCfg (x.map e) = (M.initCfg x).liftSymbols e := by
  apply Cfg.ext <;> rfl

/-- Space is preserved exactly: the head trajectories are the same.

**Proof sketch.** Unfold the visited sets and rewrite with `liftSymbols_runFrom`. -/
lemma MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_spaceUsed [DecidableEq Γ] (M : MultiTapeTM k Bool State)
    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Bool} (c : Cfg k Bool State x) (t : ℕ) :
    (M.liftSymbols e).spaceUsed (c.liftSymbols e) t = M.spaceUsed c t := by
  simp [MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape, MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead,
    MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom]

end Lift

/-- The `FinTM` layer of the lift. -/
def FinTM.liftSymbols {Γ : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (M : FinTM Bool) (e : Bool ↪ Γ) : FinTM Γ :=
  ⟨M.k, M.State, M.tm.liftSymbols e⟩

/-- A `Bool` machine computing `f` computes `f` via `e` when lifted, in the same time:
the form `Turing.FinTM.alphabet_reduction` consumes.

**Proof sketch.** Rewrite the lifted run from the lifted start with
`liftSymbols_initCfg` and `liftSymbols_runFrom`; halting and the mapped output follow. -/
theorem FinTM.liftSymbols_computesFunInTimeVia {Γ : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (M : FinTM Bool)
    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {f : List Bool → List Bool} {T : ℕ → ℕ} (h : M.ComputesFunInTime f T) :
    (M.liftSymbols e).ComputesFunInTimeVia e f T := by
  intro x
  have hx := (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mp (h x)
  refine (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr ?_
  change ((M.tm.liftSymbols e).runFrom ((M.tm.liftSymbols e).initCfg (x.map e)) _).state = none ∧
    ((M.tm.liftSymbols e).runFrom ((M.tm.liftSymbols e).initCfg (x.map e)) _).output = _
  rw [MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_initCfg, MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom]
  exact ⟨hx.1, congrArg (List.map e) hx.2⟩

/-! ### Overlays: a lifted run that keeps the rich frame (§12.8 fill, R8.0b)

`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom` transports a `Bool` run along `e` only from a
configuration that is a lift everywhere. A dedicated digit tape inside a rich host has rich
neighbours and a rich input. The overlay keeps the rich configuration's cells wherever the
`Bool` run agrees with their decoding, so a lifted run of an input-oblivious, blank-free
table transports from an arbitrary rich start. -/

section Overlay

/-- **Decoding inverts the embedding** (design §12.8a): a symbol that decodes to `b` is
`e b`. -/
theorem decodeBool_eq_some {Γ : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (γ : Γ) (b : Bool)
    (h : decodeBool e γ = some b) : γ = e b := by
  unfold decodeBool at h
  split_ifs at h with h1 h2 <;> simp_all

/-- **A lifted delimited word is the delimited word of the lift** (design §12.8a §1,
Part B). -/
theorem FinTM.bufferTape_map {Γ : Type} (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (w : List Bool) (p : ℤ) :
    FinTM.bufferTape (w.map e) p = (FinTM.bufferTape w p).map e := by
  unfold FinTM.bufferTape
  split_ifs <;> simp

/-- **A lifted delimited word decodes to the word** (design §12.8a), delimiters
included. -/
theorem FinTM.bufferTape_map_decode {Γ : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ)
    (w : List Bool) (p : ℤ) :
    (FinTM.bufferTape (w.map e) p).bind (decodeBool e) = FinTM.bufferTape w p := by
  by_cases hp : 0 ≤ p
  · simp only [FinTM.bufferTape, hp, if_true, List.getElem?_map]
    cases w[p.toNat]? <;> simp
  · simp [FinTM.bufferTape, hp]

/-- **The overlay of a `Bool` configuration on a rich one** (design §12.8a, R8.0b). Control,
input position and heads are the lift's. A cell where `c` agrees with the decoding of `D`
keeps `D`'s symbol; any other cell is `c`'s, mapped by `e`. The output is `D`'s followed by
the lift's. -/
def Cfg.liftOver {k : ℕ} {Γ Q : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Γ}
    {x' : List Bool} (hx : x'.length = x.length) (D : Cfg k Γ Q x) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x') :
    Cfg k Γ Q x :=
  ⟨(c.liftSymbols e).state, Fin.cast (by simp [hx]) (c.liftSymbols e).inputPos,
    fun j p => if c.workTapes j p = (D.workTapes j p).bind (decodeBool e) then D.workTapes j p
      else (c.liftSymbols e).workTapes j p,
    (c.liftSymbols e).workTapePos, D.output ++ (c.liftSymbols e).output⟩

/-- **One lifted step commutes with the overlay** (design §12.8a, R8.0b), for a table that
ignores its input and never writes a blank.

**Proof sketch.** The lifted table reads the overlay's cells through `decodeBool e`, which
returns `c`'s cells; input-obliviousness removes the input read. A written cell is a digit,
so it agrees with its own decoding exactly where `D`'s decoding already held it. -/
theorem MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step_over {k : ℕ} {Γ Q : Type} [DecidableEq Γ]
    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (N : MultiTapeTM k Bool Q)
    (hin : ∀ q inp inp' work, N.tr q inp work = N.tr q inp' work)
    (hnb : ∀ q inp work j, ((N.tr q inp work).workTapes j).1 ≠ some none)
    {x : List Γ} {x' : List Bool} (hx : x'.length = x.length)
    (D : Cfg k Γ Q x) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x') :
    (N.liftSymbols e).step (Cfg.liftOver e hx D c) = Cfg.liftOver e hx D (N.step c) := by
  cases hs : c.state with
  | none =>
    have : (Cfg.liftOver e hx D c).state = none := hs
    rw [MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt this, MultiTapeTM.step_of_halt hs]
  | some q =>
    have hL : (Cfg.liftOver e hx D c).state = some q := hs
    have hw : (fun j => ((Cfg.liftOver e hx D c).workTapeSymbols j).bind (decodeBool e)) =
        c.workTapeSymbols := by
      funext j
      simp only [Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Cfg.liftOver, Cfg.liftSymbols]
      split_ifs with h
      · exact h.symm
      · cases c.workTapes j (c.workTapePos j) <;> simp
    unfold MultiTapeTM.step
    rw [hL, hs]
    dsimp only
    change ((N.tr q ((Cfg.liftOver e hx D c).inputSymbol.bind (decodeBool e))
      fun j => ((Cfg.liftOver e hx D c).workTapeSymbols j).bind (decodeBool e)).liftSymbols
        e).apply (Cfg.liftOver e hx D c) = _
    rw [hw, hin q _ c.inputSymbol]
    have hnb' := hnb q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols
    generalize N.tr q c.inputSymbol c.workTapeSymbols = a at hnb'
    apply Cfg.ext
    · rfl
    · apply Fin.ext
      simp only [Action.apply, Cfg.liftOver, Action.liftSymbols, Cfg.liftSymbols, Fin.coe_cast,
        moveInputPos]
      split_ifs <;> simp <;> omega
    · funext j p
      simp only [Action.apply, Action.liftSymbols, Cfg.liftOver, Cfg.liftSymbols]
      cases ha : (a.workTapes j).1 with
      | none => simp
      | some s =>
        have hs' : s ≠ none := fun h => hnb' j (by rw [ha, h])
        obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := Option.ne_none_iff_exists'.mp hs'
        simp only [Option.map_some]
        by_cases hp : p = c.workTapePos j
        · subst hp
          simp only [Function.update_self]
          split_ifs with h
          · cases hD : D.workTapes j (c.workTapePos j) with
            | none => simp [hD] at h
            | some γ =>
              simp only [hD, Option.bind_some] at h
              rw [decodeBool_eq_some e γ b h.symm]
          · rfl
        · simp [Function.update_of_ne hp]
    · rfl
    · simp only [Action.apply, Action.liftSymbols, Cfg.liftOver, Cfg.liftSymbols,
        List.map_append, List.append_assoc]
      cases a.output <;> rfl

/-- **The overlay transport over whole runs** (design §12.8a, R8.0b): the sibling of
`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom` that keeps the rich frame.

**Proof sketch.** The one-step lemma, iterated by `Function.Semiconj.iterate_right`. -/
theorem MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom_over {k : ℕ} {Γ Q : Type} [DecidableEq Γ]
    (e : Bool ↪ Γ) (N : MultiTapeTM k Bool Q)
    (hin : ∀ q inp inp' work, N.tr q inp work = N.tr q inp' work)
    (hnb : ∀ q inp work j, ((N.tr q inp work).workTapes j).1 ≠ some none)
    {x : List Γ} {x' : List Bool} (hx : x'.length = x.length)
    (D : Cfg k Γ Q x) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x') (t : ℕ) :
    (N.liftSymbols e).runFrom (Cfg.liftOver e hx D c) t =
      Cfg.liftOver e hx D (N.runFrom c t) :=
  (Function.Semiconj.iterate_right (f := Cfg.liftOver e hx D)
    (fun c => (MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_step_over e N hin hnb hx D c).symm) t c).symm

/-- **The decoded `Bool` shadow of a rich configuration** (design §12.8a, R8.0b): cells
decoded (a foreign symbol reads as blank), the input replaced by a `Bool` word of the same
length, the output empty. -/
def Cfg.decodeSymbols {k : ℕ} {Γ Q : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ) {x : List Γ}
    (D : Cfg k Γ Q x) : Cfg k Bool Q (x.map fun _ => false) :=
  ⟨D.state, Fin.cast (by simp) D.inputPos, fun j p => (D.workTapes j p).bind (decodeBool e),
    D.workTapePos, []⟩

/-- **Every rich configuration is the overlay of its shadow on itself** (design §12.8a,
R8.0b), so the overlay transport applies from an arbitrary rich start.

**Proof sketch.** Field by field; a cell always agrees with its own decoding. -/
theorem Cfg.liftOver_decodeSymbols {k : ℕ} {Γ Q : Type} [DecidableEq Γ] (e : Bool ↪ Γ)
    {x : List Γ} (D : Cfg k Γ Q x) : Cfg.liftOver e (by simp) D (Cfg.decodeSymbols e D) = D := by
  apply Cfg.ext
  · rfl
  · apply Fin.ext; rfl
  · funext j p; simp [Cfg.liftOver, Cfg.decodeSymbols]
  · rfl
  · simp [Cfg.liftOver, Cfg.decodeSymbols, Cfg.liftSymbols]

end Overlay

end Turing
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/Embed.lean (at the gate head) =====

```
/-
